title: Business Development Analyst
description: GUIDESOURCE Business Development Researcher – Buy-and-Build Origination (Remote, Full-Time) About Guidesource Guidesource is a UK-based deal origination firm. We help acquisitive, founder-led businesses grow through acquisition by finding off-market companies for them to buy before those companies reach advisers or the open market. We run a systematic origination function for clients who have the appetite to acquire but no in-house team to source deals. We are growing our outbound engine and are hiring a full-time Business Development Researcher to power it. The Role This is a research and outreach role at the heart of our growth. You will build our pipeline of prospective clients: UK businesses that are actively acquiring and likely to keep acquiring. You will find them, research them, and run personalised email outreach to open conversations. This is not a generic mass-mailing role. Quality of targeting and personalisation is what makes it work. Day to day you will: • Find acquisition-active UK SMEs using sources such as Companies House, the trade and business press, lender and funding announcements, and LinkedIn. • Qualify each company against our target profile: founder-led or owner-managed, operating in a fragmented sector, with at least one acquisition in the last three years and signs they intend to do more. • Enrich each target: identify the right decision-maker, find a verified email and LinkedIn profile, and capture the specific event (an acquisition, a funding round, a stated plan, a key hire) that justifies the outreach. • Write personalised first-touch email s in our house style: direct, founder-to-founder, specific, no fluff. • Send and manage outreach from our company email aliases, tracking replies and follow-ups. • Keep our master tracker clean and accurate: log every company, contact, send, reply and status, with no duplicates. What We Are Looking For Essential: • Excellent written English. Your email s must read naturally and professionally, not like a template. This is the single most important requirement. • Strong research skills and genuine curiosity. You enjoy digging into companies and finding the detail others miss. • Commercial common sense. You can look at a company and form a view on whether it fits our profile and why. • Comfortable with high-volume, accurate work. You can run consistent outreach week after week without quality slipping. • Self-managing and reliable. You hit targets, keep records clean, and communicate clearly about progress and blockers. • Familiar with tools such as LinkedIn, Gmail, Google Sheets or Excel, and lead-research platforms (e.g. Apollo). Training will be given on our specific process. Nice to have: • Previous experience in B2B lead generation, sales development, recruitment research, or M&A / corporate research. • An understanding of mergers, acquisitions, or private equity, or a strong willingness to learn it quickly. • Experience writing or editing professional email s for a Western business audience. What Success Looks Like We measure this role on outcomes, not just activity. In the first three months you will build a steady, well-qualified pipeline and run consistent personalised outreach. Success is measured by the number of well-targeted companies researched, the quality of personalisation, and ultimately the replies and conversations your outreach generates. Practicalities • Location: Fully remote. You can be based anywhere, but you must have a reliable internet connection and a quiet place to work. • Hours: Full-time. Some overlap with UK business hours is required for coordination. • Reporting: You will work directly with the founders. • Compensation: [Add your salary here] - strong bonus structure How to Apply Send a short note telling us why this role suits you, along with your CV.

description: Job Title: Mortgage Loan Processor (DSCR / Non-QM Focus) Employment Type: Full-Time Company: NEXA Mortgage, LLC Position Overview We are seeking a detail-oriented Mortgage Loan Processor with strong DSCR and investment property experience to support a high-volume pipeline. Key Responsibilities Review new DSCR and Non-QM files for completeness and accuracy before submission. Submit files to underwriting and manage each loan through to clear to close. Review conditional approvals and prepare a clear, organized list of conditions. Communicate directly with borrowers to request and collect documentation, and explain underwriting conditions in plain, professional language. Follow up persistently with borrowers, third parties, and vendors to clear outstanding items. Order and track appraisals, title, insurance, and payoffs, and coordinate with those providers throughout the file. Upload and organize all documentation in the LOS and keep compliance requirements satisfied. Work side by side with the Loan Originator to resolve conditions quickly and keep every file moving toward closing. Qualifications Prior experience as a Mortgage Loan Processor, with hands-on DSCR and Non-QM processing strongly preferred. Working knowledge of DSCR ratio calculations, rent schedules, and entity-vested investment property files. Experience processing conventional full doc loans under TRID, plus bank statement income loans. Familiarity with wholesale lender portals and submission processes. Strong written and verbal communication and the ability to work directly with borrowers. Highly organized with excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage many files at once. Comfortable in an LOS and document management platforms (LendingPad experience a plus). Key Traits for Success Confident processing DSCR files independently from submission to clear to close. job_title: TikTok Social Media Manager — Part-Time, Philippines-Based | DTC E-Commerce Brand | $350–$550/mo
description: Is This You? You wake up and the first thing you check is your For You Page — not because you're bored, but because you're studying it. You know what's converting this week. You know which sounds are peaking. You know the difference between a hook that stops thumbs and a hook that makes people actually watch past three seconds. You've run TikTok for a real brand — not just your personal account, not just a side project. You've posted content, watched the numbers, formed a hypothesis, changed the approach, and done it again. You don't need someone to explain the algorithm to you. You need someone to let you work. If that's you, keep reading. If you're still figuring out TikTok while managing it for brands, this isn't the right fit. What You'll Own • TikTok is your primary responsibility. You'll plan, script, edit, post, and iterate on content for 3 DTC product brands in the US natural goods space — bar soap, tallow skincare, and freeze-dried pet treats. Footage comes from the brand owner and UGC creators; your job is to make it perform. Expect 2–4 posts per week per active brand, scaling as the brands grow. • Build and maintain a content calendar — and actually hit it, without being reminded. • Write hooks that compete. Every video starts with a line or a visual that earns the next three seconds. You'll be judged on this. • Select audio strategically — trending sounds, original audio, voiceover decisions. You'll know why you chose what you chose. • Structure videos for completion rate: pacing, editing rhythm, CTA placement. CapCut or similar is your tool. • Repurpose UGC and existing video assets into original-feeling content — recut, reframed, re-scored. You know how to transform raw footage so the algorithm treats it as new, not duplicate. Uncut re-uploads are not an option here. • Use native TikTok formats — Duet, Stitch, Green Screen — strategically to extend reach, respond to trends, and generate engagement without starting from zero every time. • Repurpose top-performing TikToks for Instagram Reels. Manage Facebook pages (posting, community replies, basic scheduling). • Monitor comments and DMs across platforms; flag anything that needs owner attention. • Coordinate with TikTok Shop: product link setup, affiliate outreach awareness, live selling scheduling when applicable. • Track your own metrics — reach, watch time, saves, shares, follower growth — and deliver a clear weekly summary. No vanity-metric spin. Just honest numbers and what you're doing about them. • Proactively bring content ideas, trend observations, and competitive intel to the owner. Don't wait to be asked. What We're Looking For Hard Requirements • Minimum 2 years managing TikTok for a US-market brand or agency client (product brands preferred) • Demonstrated results: you can show before/after data or real account growth you drove • Fluent written English — you'll write scripts, captions, and direct communications with the brand owner • Proficient in CapCut or equivalent mobile/desktop editing tool • Available for async communication; able to flag urgent items in real time during PH business hours • Reliable and deadline-driven — you treat posting schedules like commitments, not suggestions • Comfortable working with minimal supervision on a fully remote team Strong Advantages • TikTok Shop experience: product linking, affiliate program coordination, LIVE commerce awareness • Experience in natural products, wellness, pet, or handcrafted goods categories • Proficiency with native TikTok formats: Duet, Stitch, Green Screen — used as deliberate reach and engagement tools, not just features • Instagram Reels native editing (not just cross-posting) • Familiarity with US consumer behavior and the DTC e-commerce landscape ?? TikTok Compliance & Platform Intelligence — Non-Negotiable This section matters more than most postings acknowledge, so it gets its own block. These brands operate in regulated-adjacent categories: skincare, pet nutrition, personal care. One compliant-looking post with the wrong claim, a banned audio track, or a policy violation the owner didn't know about can cost a suppressed account, a restricted shop, or worse. We need someone who treats TikTok's Terms of Service, Community Guidelines, and Commerce Policies as required reading — not fine print. That means: • You track policy updates. You know what changed in the last 90 days and what it means for product-based content. • You flag risks before posting — not after the fact. • You understand what can and cannot be said in TikTok Shop product listings, video captions, and on-screen text for health and wellness products. • You know which claim types trigger review, suppression, or removal, and you keep the brand far away from those lines. • You understand TikTok's duplicate content detection — and know how to properly re-edit, reframe, and re-score UGC or existing footage so it registers as original. Re-uploading uncut videos is a fast way to get suppressed. You don't do that. • You can explain your compliance reasoning when asked. Candidates who treat this as a checkbox will not advance. Candidates who treat this as a professional discipline will. What You'll Get • $350–$550 USD/month, part-time (~20 hours/week) — based on experience and demonstrated results. This is a part-time engagement to start, with a clear path to full-time as the brands scale. • Fully remote. Core hours are Manila time, founders live in Philippines. No micromanagement. No daily check-in calls. You own your schedule as long as deadlines are met. • Stable, long-term engagement — this is not a project hire. The right person grows with us. As posting volume increases and results compound, the scope (and pay) expands. • Clear scope. You won't be asked to do customer service, inventory, or tasks outside your lane. • Direct access to the brand owner — decisions get made fast, feedback is real, and good work gets recognized. How to Apply Send the following: 1. A brief intro (3–5 sentences): who you are, what brands or accounts you've managed on TikTok, and one result you're proud of. 2. Links to 2–3 TikTok accounts you've managed (or specific videos if the accounts are no longer live). If the work is under NDA, describe it — but be specific. 3. Your answer to this question. This is required. No answer = no consideration: "Name one TikTok rule, policy change, or platform update from the last 6 months that could affect a US e-commerce brand selling physical products. How would you handle it — both in terms of your content approach and what you'd communicate to the brand owner?" Answer in your own words. A vague, generic or AI-generated response tells us everything we need to know. These are small, real brands built around products people genuinely love. We're not filling a seat — we're looking for someone who takes pride in their work, wants a stable long-term role, and is ready to grow alongside us. If that's you, we'd love to hear from you.

title: UX/UI Web Designer
description: *Web Designer (UX/UI) — Gig / Part-time / Full-time* Boutique Branding Studio — Netherlands --- *About the Role* We're a boutique branding studio based in the Netherlands. We work at the intersection of brand strategy, identity, and digital execution. The websites we build are not afterthoughts to a brand project, they are the brand, made interactive. We're looking for a Web Designer who leads with structure and ends with craft. Someone who opens a new project by thinking about pages, flows, and systems, not colours and typefaces. The visual execution matters enormously, but it comes last. You'll join a small team on a gig basis, with a clear path to part-time and full-time for the right person. You'll own the design process from sitemap to hand-off, working alongside our brand leads and Webflow developer. --- *Who You Are* Before you are a designer, you are a systems thinker. You map information before you design screens. You wireframe to solve problems, not to sketch rough ideas. When you look at a website brief, your first instinct is to ask: what does this site need to do, how should it be structured, and how will someone move through it? You understand the web as a medium, not a canvas. You think about scroll behaviour, states, responsiveness, and hierarchy the way a developer thinks about logic: it either works or it doesn't. You're not a graphic designer who builds websites on the side. Web design is your specialism. It's where your thinking lives. --- *What You'll Do* — Translate briefs and brand strategy into sitemaps and content architecture before a single screen is designed — Build wireframes that define structure, hierarchy, and user flow with enough detail that they could be critiqued and approved on their own — Design full website concepts in Figma, desktop and mobile, using consistent components and a system-first approach — Build and maintain design systems and component libraries that scale across pages and projects — Hand off clean, structured Figma files to our Webflow developer with zero ambiguity — Work closely with brand leads from briefing through to final design, contributing to conceptual direction where needed --- *What We're Not Looking For* A graphic designer who can also do web. Someone who jumps to visual design before the structure is solved. Someone who designs pages in isolation without thinking about the system they belong to. Someone who needs direction at every step. If your portfolio is full of beautiful screens with no evidence of the thinking behind them, this is not the right role. --- *What We're Looking For* Required: — 5+ years specialising in web design — not general graphic, brand, or print design — A genuine process: sitemap ? wireframe ? visual design, every time — Strong information architecture skills — you can define page structure, navigation logic, and content hierarchy from a brief — Wireframes that stand on their own — detailed, annotated, and used as a real tool for alignment — Expert Figma skills: components, auto layout, variants, design systems, developer hand-off — A systems mindset — you think in reusable parts, not one-off pages — Deep understanding of web UX: conversion logic, scroll behaviour, mobile-first thinking, interactive states — Portfolio of live marketing and corporate websites that show process, not just output — Clear, proactive communicator in English Nice to have: — Familiarity with Webflow, knowing how your designs will be built makes you a better designer — Experience building or maintaining full design systems across multiple projects — Conceptual contribution to brand and campaign work that feeds into web — Micro-interaction or animation thinking at the wireframe stage --- *How We Work Together* A project starts with a briefing — sometimes strategic, sometimes a brand deep-dive, often both. From there, you lead: sitemap first, wireframes second, visual design third. You'll work closely with our brand leads and Webflow developer at each stage. Client communication stays with the studio. Your job is to design something that works and looks considered, then hand it off clearly. We're a small team. We don't micromanage, and we don't chase. We expect you to ask the right questions early, raise blockers when they appear, and deliver work that doesn't need explaining. --- *Compensation* Hourly rate is based on experience and portfolio. title: Operations Assistant for Growing U.S. E-commerce Store | Shopify, CRM & Customer Support
job_title: Operations Assistant for Growing U.S. E-commerce Store | Shopify, CRM & Customer Support
description: Hi! I’m looking for a reliable full-time E-commerce Operations Assistant to help with daily operations for a growing online-only store in the U.S. market. We sell high-value products in categories such as outdoor living, e-bikes, saunas, off-grid products, power products, and lifestyle products, with more brands and product categories being added over time. This is not a simple one-product dropshipping store. We work with multiple brands and suppliers, and many products are shipped directly from suppliers or manufacturers. Each brand can have different prices, margins, shipping rules, lead times, product details, warranties, return policies, and supplier requirements. Because of this, attention to detail is very important. A wrong price, wrong product detail, missed follow-up, or incorrect promise to a customer can create serious problems. This is a full-time position, not a “work whenever you want” role. Since this position involves customer email s, SMS, calls, supplier follow-ups, abandoned checkout follow-ups, Shopify tasks, and order updates, you must be available during agreed U.S. business hours, ideally between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Eastern Time. We are still in the early stages as a business, but our goal is to grow and scale. We are looking for someone long-term, reliable, committed, detail-oriented, and proactive who can grow with us. As the business grows, tasks may become more specialized, but this role requires someone who can understand a little bit of everything at the beginning. Responsibilities and hourly rate can increase based on performance, reliability, communication, and the value you bring to the company. Main tasks may include: * Responding to customer email s, SMS, and calls in English. * Making and answering customer calls when needed. * Following up with customers about quotes, pending payments, abandoned checkouts, delivery updates, product questions, and order issues. * Following up with suppliers about stock, pricing, shipping, product details, lead times, tracking, freight delivery, warranty cases, and order updates. * Updating customers about order status, delivery updates, supplier responses, delays, and next steps. * Checking product prices, supplier costs, margins, shipping costs, MAP rules, and competitor pricing. * Comparing our prices with U.S. competitors. * Using a VPN when needed to view U.S. pricing, competitor websites, and product availability. * Helping with Shopify product uploads and product updates. * Creating, editing, and improving Shopify product listings using supplier information. * Reviewing product titles, descriptions, specifications, images, SEO titles, meta descriptions, tags, collections, warranty details, shipping details, and product page accuracy. * Identifying missing product information, incorrect specs, weak descriptions, pricing issues, or product pages that need improvement. * Keeping CRM sheets and internal spreadsheets organized. * Updating customer notes, supplier notes, order notes, lead status, and follow-up status. * Helping with warranty, return, cancellation, delivery, and supplier communication. * Assisting with documentation for warranty claims, returns, delivery issues, disputes, and chargebacks when needed. * Preparing draft responses for customer issues when needed. * Following SOPs, training videos, examples, and instructions carefully. * Suggesting improvements to processes, product pages, customer communication, follow-ups, spreadsheets, or SOPs after learning how the business works. You will not be expected to know everything on day one. The first week will focus on training, onboarding, and learning how our process works. We may use Zoom calls, Google Meet calls, training videos, SOPs, examples, and internal documents to explain tasks clearly. I prefer someone who asks questions before guessing, especially when dealing with customers, suppliers, pricing, shipping, returns, warranties, or order issues. Important: You should not promise customers exact delivery dates unless they are confirmed. You should not approve refunds, returns, cancellations, discounts, disputes, or compensation unless management specifically authorizes it. You must be careful when checking prices because different brands have different margins, supplier costs, shipping fees, MAP rules, and competitor pricing. Requirements: * Advanced written and spoken English for U.S. customer communication. * Confident speaking with U.S. customers by phone in clear, professional English. * Comfortable answering calls, making follow-up calls, replying to SMS, and handling customer issues professionally. * Able to communicate clearly when there is a delay, delivery concern, warranty issue, return request, or customer complaint. * Experience with Shopify, e-commerce operations, customer support, product listings, SEO edits, pricing checks, or virtual assistant work. * Experience with high-ticket e-commerce, supplier-direct shipping, freight products, warranty cases, returns, or multi-brand online stores is strongly preferred. * Experience using Google Sheets, CRM sheets, spreadsheets, or similar tools to stay organized. * Available full-time during agreed U.S. business hours, ideally between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Eastern Time. * Must have reliable internet. * Must be able to use a VPN when needed. * Strong attention to detail. * Organized and able to keep accurate notes. * Able to follow step-by-step instructions carefully. * Able to ask questions when something is unclear instead of guessing. * Able to work with urgency when a task is assigned. * Able to suggest useful ideas or improvements after understanding the business process. * Experience using Slack or similar communication tools is a plus, but not required. Examples of tasks you may receive: * “Check if this product is in stock with the supplier and confirm the shipping cost.” * “Reply to this customer asking for a delivery update.” * “Call this customer and confirm their shipping address.” * “Call or text this customer who started checkout but did not complete the order.” * “Compare our price with this competitor and calculate the margin.” * “Update the CRM sheet with the customer status and next follow-up.” * “Check if this product page is missing warranty, shipping, or specification details.” * “Upload these products to Shopify using this supplier page.” * “Review this product listing and improve the title, description, specifications, SEO title, and meta description.” * “Follow up with this supplier about tracking or freight delivery.” * “Review this customer issue and prepare a draft response.” How to apply: Please message me here if you are interested. To show that you read the full post carefully, start your message with: “Hi Chris, I can help with U.S. e-commerce operations.” Also, somewhere in your application, mention: “CRM sheet” Please do not send a generic cover letter. I want to understand your real experience, communication style, and judgment, so please answer in your own words and do not use AI-generated responses. Please include a short video recording speaking in English. This can be a Loom video, Google Drive link, or any similar link. Please make sure the link is accessible. The video will help us evaluate your spoken English, clear pronunciation, confidence, and overall communication skills when speaking with U.S. customers. Please do not read directly from AI-generated text or scripts. We want to hear you speaking naturally in your own words so we can better understand your real communication style and confidence level. Please try not to read directly from a script. It is better if the video feels natural and conversational, using your own words and ideas. This helps us understand your real communication style, confidence, and how you would speak with customers. In your message or video, please answer these questions: 1. Have you worked with Shopify, customer service, or e-commerce operations before? Explain briefly. 2. Have you worked with high-ticket e-commerce products, supplier-direct shipping, freight items, or multi-brand online stores before? If yes, please explain your experience. 3. Are you comfortable speaking with U.S. customers by phone in English? 4. Are you available full-time during U.S. business hours, ideally between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Eastern Time? 5. Have you used Google Sheets, CRM sheets, or spreadsheets to manage customer/order information? 6. Have you helped create, edit, or improve Shopify product listings before? If yes, what parts have you handled? For example: product titles, descriptions, specifications, images, SEO titles, meta descriptions, tags, collections, or pricing. 7. If you have worked with other e-commerce stores before, what is one process, system, product page, or customer communication workflow you helped improve? 8. A customer asks for an exact delivery date, but the supplier only gave an estimated transit time. How would you respond? 9. Before telling a customer that a product is in stock, what would you check? 10. If a customer asks for a refund, discount, cancellation, return, dispute update, or compensation, what would you do before confirming anything? 11. Are you able to use a VPN to check U.S. competitor pricing and product availability? 12. What is your expected hourly rate? We are looking for someone who does more than just complete assigned tasks. We value someone who can think, ask good questions, suggest improvements, and help us improve our systems as we grow. Applications that do not follow these instructions will not be considered. Thanks! Chris

description: ABOUT THE PROJECT AI Bands is a fast-growing fitness tech startup building the future of connected workouts. WHAT YOU WILL DELIVER • Two Fully Assembled Prototype Units: Clean soldering, solid wire management, and securely housed electronics inside the ABS enclosures integrated seamlessly with the bands and handles. • Flashed BLE Firmware: ESP32 microcontrollers flashed with baseline Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) firmware to stream data strings (spec sheet provided upon hire). • Component Verification: Proven sensor output data streams from the load cell, HX711, and MPU-6050.Build Documentation: Clear photo updates log recorded at each stage of the wiring and assembly. • Engineering Notes: Brief written summaries detailing any component substitutions, technical challenges, or hardware optimization suggestions. • Secure Packaging & Courier Handoff: Finished prototypes securely packed and shipped to our corporate address in the US (All international shipping costs are covered in full by AI Bands via Wise). SKILLS REQUIRED • Precision Bench Skills: Professional soldering, wiring configuration, and basic troubleshooting of low-power small electronics. • Microcontroller Literacy: Hands-on experience flashing and debugging ESP32 or Arduino environments. • Spec Sheet Competence: Fully comfortable reading schematic lists, pinout guides, and technical build specifications. • Documentation Discipline: Organized habits when logging build milestones and capturing clean progress photos. • Prior Build History: You must have physical, real-world examples or photos of functional hardware or DIY electronics you have built with your own hands. NICE TO HAVE (But not required): • Custom BLE firmware optimization experience. • Access to a 3D printer for custom interior component brackets or housing modifications. • Familiarity with load cell strain-gauge calibration properties. • Prior experience building wearable technology or fitness tracking hardware. YOU ARE A GREAT FIT IF YOU: • Have actually built real things that turn on—not just simulations on paper. • Communicate proactively and transparently the same day a part is defective, delayed, or requires a technical substitution. • Take true ownership of your workspace and meet timeline benchmarks without daily oversight. • Can interpret a technical spec accurately while using solid judgment when minor structural details are open-ended. description: Job Description: x86 System Boot Loader Designer Position Overview: We are seeking a talented and experienced x86/ARM System Boot Loader Designer to join our team. Responsibilities: Develop and design the boot loader software for x86/ARM-based computer systems, including BIOS and UEFI firmware. Implement low-level programming and optimization techniques to enhance boot performance and reduce boot time. Customize boot loaders to support specific hardware configurations and system requirements. Debug and troubleshoot boot-related issues, both independently and in collaboration with the firmware development team. Conduct thorough testing and validation of the boot loader software to ensure its reliability and compatibility with target systems. Document design specifications, architectural diagrams, and code structures for future reference and knowledge sharing. Collaborate with the software engineering team to integrate the boot loader with the operating system and other software components. Provide technical support and guidance to internal teams and external stakeholders regarding boot loader-related queries and issues. Qualifications: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Strong understanding of x86 architecture and system booting processes. Proficiency in low-level programming languages, such as Assembly and C/C++. Experience with BIOS and UEFI firmware development, including familiarity with related standards and protocols. In-depth knowledge of boot loader technologies, including boot stages, boot protocols, and boot loader customization. Familiarity with system-level debugging tools, such as JTAG, GDB, and kernel debuggers. Experience with firmware development tools, such as Intel System Studio, UEFI Development Kit (UDK), or similar. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to debug complex boot-related issues. Excellent communication and collaboration skills to work effectively within cross-functional teams. Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet project deadlines. Preferred Qualifications: Prior experience in designing boot loaders for embedded systems or real-time operating systems. Knowledge of security features and considerations related to booting and firmware development. Familiarity with virtualization technologies, such as Intel VT-x or AMD-V. Experience with Linux kernel development, Linux containers, and knowledge of containerization technologies like Docker or Kubernetes. Familiarity with the FlexBuild tool for building Linux systems or similar build automation tools. Join our team and contribute to the development of cutting-edge x86-based computer systems. As an x86/ARM System Boot Loader Designer, you will have the opportunity to work on complex firmware development projects and play a vital role in shaping the booting experience of our products, leveraging your knowledge and experience with Linux Kernel, Linux containers, and FlexBuild tool.

title: Editor for a Moto-Vlog Style YouTube Channel
job_title: Editor for a Moto-Vlog Style YouTube Channel
description: I THINK WE MISSED A TURN: Editor for a Moto-Vlog Style YouTube Channel - TCAT Remapping Expedition 2026 Editor for a Moto-Vlog Style YouTube Channel OVERVIEW - Craig Luke is a Canadian Moto-Vlogger based in Nelson, British Columbia. He is currently riding solo, coast to coast off-road, to remap the Trans Canada Adventure Trail. 15,000 km from Grant Bay on Vancouver Island to St. John's, Newfoundland. Roughly six months on the dirt road. You are the editor who turns each journey's raw footage into a finished, upload-ready video. - This is off-road adventure motorcycling content made by riders for riders. Authentic and practical. Real Canadian backcountry travel, not influencer polish. He shoots on a lightweight Kove 450 Rally and lives on a strict $50/day budget. Footage comes off the trail and uploads via Starlink Mini from remote campsites. Every video should feel like the viewer is out there with him. - Style benchmark is Itchy Boots ---------- story-driven pacing built around solo travel, geographic progression, map tracking and the raw beauty of the trail. Not hyper-edited visual noise. - Publish cadence is once every three days to start. Turnaround is within 48 hours from the moment a journey's assets are ready. THE ROLE - We outline each episode in a shared Google Sheet. An episode may cover one day or several days. You build one finished episode per outline. - We engage you video by video to start. - If we like your work and we are working well together, we build a longer-term relationship from there. - We want a go-to editor for the entire 15,000km project across Canada and beyond. - The production hub is this Google Sheet: ---------- REVIEW THE CHANNEL FIRST - Watch the current channel for context and style: ---------- - We want you to match the rider-to-rider feel and then raise the bar. - Come with ideas. Better pacing, cleaner sound design, sharper color, smarter cutaways, stronger hooks and openings, chapter markers, retention editing. - Tell us what you would do differently and why. REFERENCE VIDEOS (watch before you start) - Study these before your first edit. They show the target. Match the pacing, energy and storytelling. Do not copy shot for shot. - Style we are aiming for: youtu.be/t8R4xB9k6xI - Reference: youtu.be/6cmY8qEdvIM - Channel benchmark: Itchy Boots, ---------- SOURCE FOOTAGE - Craig shoots each day on three cameras. - Insta360 X4 Air. 360 capture for reframing and impossible angles. 8K. - Insta360 GO Ultra. Mounted POV and cube shots. - Phone. Handheld and talking-to-camera footage. WHERE EVERYTHING LIVES - Google Sheet (production hub). Every episode outlines lives here. The narrative spine, titles, descriptions, tags, notes, locations and track links. An outline may span multiple days. This is your starting point for every episode. - Google Drive day folders. Raw footage from the three cameras, photos of people and scenery, Craig's voiceover and in most cases the route map video file. - ---------- . The route map is usually dropped into the Drive folder as a finished video. In some cases over the next two weeks you may need to grab the route video for the day from ---------- yourself. Craig is moving toward providing it automatically in the folder. - Insta360 Studio app. Where you reframe and export the 360 footage before Premiere, or you use the Insta360 plugin inside Premiere instead. THE 360 WORKFLOW - You handle the 360 footage one of two ways. - Reframe and export the 360 footage in the Insta360 Studio app first, then bring it into Adobe Premiere Pro. - Or use the Adobe Premiere Pro Insta360 plugin to import and reframe the .insv files directly inside Premiere. - Pick the path your machine handles cleanly. Everything finishes in Premiere. WHAT YOU BUILD - One finished episode per outline. - The route map worked into the video. Most days the map video is already in the Drive folder. Occasionally you pull it from ---------- . - Craig's voiceover laid in as the spine of the story. - The pre-made intro and outro applied to every video. - People and scenery photos worked in as cutaways and b-roll where they fit the story. EDIT APPROACH - Follow the outline in the Google Sheet as the spine. It tells you where Craig was, where he was going and what happened. - Cut for story first, polish second. The ride is the star. Find the arc. Geographic progress, the struggle, the breakdown, the triumph, the camp routine. - Keep it honest. No fake drama. Sound like a rider, not a brand. - Reframe the X4 360 footage to land the action. Use the small POV cam for mounted shots. Use the phone for Craig to camera. - Pacing and sound design. Balance voiceover and music against crisp engine audio, wind and ambient nature sound. Build tension on technical trail. Go cinematic and calm at camp. The voice stays clear and on top. REQUIRED SKILLS AND HARDWARE - Expert editor in Adobe Premiere Pro. This is the only editor we use. We want every project built in Premiere so we can bring editing in-house later. - Insta360 workflow. Reframe and stabilize 360 footage cleanly. Run the Insta360 Reframe plugin in Premiere or reframe and export in the Insta360 Studio app first. - Handle heavy 4K and 8K files smoothly. - Audio layering and sound design. Balance voiceover, camera audio, engine sound and music so the voice stays crystal clear. - Story editing. Find the narrative arc in hours of raw trail footage without over-editing. The Itchy Boots flow. - Strong English comprehension. You follow written outlines and check on-screen metadata against what actually happened on camera. - Reliable communication and on-time delivery inside the 48 hour window. - Fast internet and a high-spec machine. You will pull heavy 8K and 4K files from Google Drive and the Insta360 cloud. NICE TO HAVE (strong bonus, not required) - Map and motion graphics. Generate route paths from GPX using Google Earth Studio, After Effects or a dedicated mapping plugin. In most cases the route map is provided for you. Relive supplies the motion graphics if they come on as a sponsor. Otherwise we build it through Google Maps or another option. This is a real plus if you can do it. - After Effects for titles, lower thirds and clean motion graphics. - Color grading in Lumetri. - Thumbnail design. - Experience editing travel, moto, outdoor or adventure content. WHAT WE LOOK FOR IN YOU - Detail focused. You catch the small things. - Self-managed. We do not track your hours. You hold the milestones and the quality. - A storyteller, not just a button pusher. - In it for the long haul. We want one editor for the whole expedition. DELIVERY AND APPROVAL - Drop two files back into the journey's Google Drive folder. The Adobe Premiere master project file (once approved and finalized) and the finished video file. - Do not upload anything to YouTube. We handle that ourselves for now. We bring you into that once we have worked together for a while. - Use the title, description and tags from the Google Sheet. If Craig covered something on camera that was not in the outline, update the metadata to match what actually happened. - Tell us the episode is ready for review. All of this inside the 48 hour turnaround window. COMPENSATION AND WORK TERMS - We are a Canadian company. All pay is in Canadian dollars (CAD). - Structure. Paid per completed video. One finished longform episode, 15 to 20 minutes. - Trial rate. $65 CAD per video for your first 3 videos. This is a paid trial so we both confirm the fit. - Standard rate. $100 CAD per video from video 4 onward, once the trial passes review and we are working well together. - Growth bonus. When the channel hits 20,000 subscribers you earn a bonus on every video on top of your per-video rate. - Performance bonus. Once the channel revenue grows we add a bonus tied to views on the videos you personally edit. This is added to your base, never in place of it. - Monthly retainer. When the channel is profitable we are willing to move you to a monthly retainer plus bonuses. - Payment schedule. Paid after each video is completed. We move to a monthly salary when the channel hits 50,000 subscribers. Paid in CAD. - Flexibility. We do not track your hours. You manage your own schedule as long as the milestones and quality hold for each delivery. - Long-term potential. We want one go-to editor for the full 15,000km project across Canada and beyond. HOW TO APPLY (read carefully) - We only hire people who pay attention to detail. Automated or copy-pasted applications get ignored. In your application include the items below. - The secret phrase. Start your message with this exact line: "I found the turn! - ITWMAT Video Editor". - Your portfolio. Links to YouTube or adventure content you personally edited. Include examples with maps or heavy voiceover. - Production ideas. After watching the channel, name two or three specific things you would do to raise the production quality. - Your project rate. Confirm our per-video structure works, or give your target rate in CAD per 15 to 20 minute finished video. - Your gear and connection. A short description of your computer specs and a screenshot of your internet download and upload speed. NEXT STEP - Watch both reference videos and the current channel, then reply with your questions on the open specs and your production ideas so we can lock everything before the first folder lands.

description: About Us We're a fast-growing Australian business finance company. We're a lean team that competes through automation — our tech stack does the work of 100 people, and we're hiring one senior person to own, extend, and improve it full-time. Our Stack (you'll work across most of this) -Zapier (advanced: code steps, webhooks, paths, error handling — not just simple Zaps) -Airtable (automations, scripting, complex base design, API) -Pipedrive CRM (API, webhooks, workflow automation) -ActiveCampaign (automations, API) -Python (Flask services deployed on Google Cloud Run) -REST APIs generally — reading API docs and building reliable integrations is the core of this job -LLM integrations (Claude / OpenAI APIs — building automations that use AI models via API) -WordPress — custom code (PHP/HTML/CSS/JS), performance optimisation (Core Web Vitals), and ongoing site management. Not just themes and plugins — you must be able to work in the code. -Google Tag Manager & tracking — GTM container setup, dataLayer coding, UTM parameter architecture, conversion tracking (including server-side / Conversions API) -Cloudflare, DNS, domains & hosting — DNS records, security settings, SSL, domain management (GoDaddy etc.), hosting environments -Softr (client portal on top of Airtable) -Plus: SMS APIs (Twilio/Sinch), Meta Conversions API, and AI voice APIs You don't need experience with every tool — but you MUST be strong on Zapier + Airtable + APIs + Python + WordPress (real coding, not just plugins), and able to learn the rest fast from documentation. What You'll Do -Build new automations and improve existing ones (lead routing, CRM workflows, client notifications, and LLM-powered automation systems) -Own our WordPress website end-to-end: performance (Core Web Vitals), custom code changes, design polish, and reliability -Own our tracking infrastructure: GTM, dataLayer, UTM architecture, and conversion tracking accuracy across Meta and Google -Manage the infrastructure layer: Cloudflare, DNS, domains, hosting, SSL, and security settings -Innovate with AI. We use LLMs heavily across our systems and expect you to stay current with new models, tools, and techniques — and to proactively propose where AI can improve or replace existing processes. "I saw this new capability and built a prototype" is the energy we pay bonuses for. -Debug production issues by finding root causes — not patching symptoms -Integrate third-party APIs by reading official documentation carefully and verifying exact parameter specs (this is a hard requirement for us — guessing at API parameters is how systems break) -Write clear documentation: every automation you ship comes with a written spec and runbook. No exceptions. -Proactively identify problems and improvements before being asked — we pay bonuses specifically for this Compensation -Base: USD $2,500–3,000/month depending on experience -Monthly performance bonus: USD $300–800 based on shipped systems that run reliably, documentation quality, and -proactive problem-finding. Opportunity to go even higher, based on performance. -Annual base increases for strong performers -Long-term, stable, full-time role — we are building for years, not months Hours Of Work Full-time, Monday–Friday, working - 9am - 6pm SYDNEY TIME. Who This Role Suits -5+ years building automations, integrations, and websites professionally — you're a senior generalist who's comfortable owning the entire technical surface of a business, not a specialist in one tool -You're a problem solver and have a high degree of attention to detail -You chase root causes, not symptoms — "I found why it breaks" instead of "I added a workaround" -You read API documentation for fun (or at least without pain) -You're genuinely excited by AI — you already use LLMs in your own workflow, follow new releases, and have built things with -AI APIs because you wanted to, not just because a client asked -You test your own work before calling it done -You communicate clearly and proactively — if something is blocked or broken, we hear it from you first -You want one stable long-term client who pays well and pays bonuses, not five gigs Who This Role Does NOT Suit -Anyone whose Zapier experience is limited to simple two-step Zaps -Anyone whose WordPress experience is page builders only (Elementor/Divi) — if you can't work directly in PHP/HTML/CSS/JS and diagnose performance issues in the code, this isn't your role -Anyone who hardcodes credentials or guesses at API parameters instead of checking docs -Anyone juggling multiple clients (we require exclusivity during work hours) -Agencies, teams, or anyone planning to subcontract any part of this work. We are hiring you, one individual — the person we interview is the person who does the work, always. Given the financial data our systems handle, subcontracting is treated as a serious breach and grounds for immediate termination. -Anyone uncomfortable with logged/audited system access — we run strict security practices (scoped credentials, audit trails). Honest builders find this boring; that's the point. Security Note (read this — it matters) We work with financial data, so we follow least-privilege access practices: you'll use your own named accounts and scoped API keys, production credentials are managed by the owner, and system activity is logged. This is standard, professional, and protects you as much as us. If that sounds reasonable, we'll get along great. SKILL REQUIREMENTS Required: -Zapier (Expert) -Airtable (Expert) -AI Tool Use — Claude Code / ChatGPT (Expert) -API Integration / REST APIs (Expert) -WordPress — custom code & performance (Advanced) -Google Tag Manager / UTM / conversion tracking (Advanced) -Python (Advanced) -HTML / CSS / JavaScript (Advanced) -Webhooks (Advanced) -Cloudflare / DNS / domain & hosting management (Intermediate–Advanced) Strongly preferred: -Pipedrive or similar CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce) -ActiveCampaign or similar (Mailchimp, Klaviyo) -Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions) -Flask or similar Python web frameworks -Meta Conversions API / server-side tracking Nice to have: -Softr / no-code app builders -Twilio / Sinch / Kixie, SMS APIs -SQL HOW TO APPLY To apply, send a message that includes ALL of the following — applications missing any item will not be read: 1. Start your message with the word "PINEAPPLE" so we know you read the full post. 2. Your 2–3 best automation/integration projects — for each: what it did, which tools/APIs were involved, and one problem you hit and how you solved it. Specific detail matters more than polish. Include links wherever possible — live websites you've built or optimised, GitHub, portfolio, or Loom walkthroughs. Claims we can verify are worth far more than claims we can't. 3. A short video introduction (3–5 minutes, camera on) — Loom or similar. Briefly: who you are, what you've built that you're proudest of, and what specifically about this role appeals to you. job_title: Junior Developer - AI-Augmented Product & Tooling Team
description: USD Pay · Long-Term · Philippines What We're Building We build AI-powered consumer products, custom developer tooling, and client solutions across multiple verticals: AI image and video generation — a mobile and web app that transforms photos into stylized artwork using generative AI. Single Flutter codebase, Firebase backend, multiple AI model integrations. Game development — interactive experiences with structured world-building and AI-assisted content generation. Prompt research and skills tooling — we built a package manager for AI agent prompts and skills that detects your repo's tech stack and ranks results accordingly. We research how prompts perform across different models, build reusable skill packages that any AI coding agent can load, and maintain a catalog of 30+ skills covering everything from security review to prompt quality self-assessment. This isn't a side project — it's a core product. MCP and agent workflow research — we actively research and build integrations using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and other emerging standards that reduce friction between developers and AI agents. We've built coordination servers that let multiple agents reserve files, message each other, and avoid conflicts. We've built tmux-based orchestration so developers can run 3-5 AI agents in parallel. When a new protocol, tool, or workflow pattern emerges, we evaluate it against real work and adopt or build what's missing. Code quality tooling for agentic development — AI agents write a lot of code fast. The bottleneck isn't speed, it's confidence. We built compiler-integrated mutation testing and code quality metrics in Rust and TypeScript — tools that use each language's native AST parser so agents and developers can trust that generated code actually works. These aren't standalone research projects; they're the quality backbone that makes high-velocity agentic development safe. Infrastructure and DevOps — Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines, private networking, infrastructure-as-code across all projects. How We Work We follow a pattern that defines the team culture: see a gap ? research what's available ? build it or adopt the best option ? ship it ? share it with the team. We needed mutation testing tuned to our languages — generic linters couldn't handle Rust's error propagation or TypeScript's union types correctly. So we built compiler-integrated tools that use each language's native AST parser. We needed AI coding agents to coordinate without stepping on each other's files. So we built an MCP coordination server and a tmux orchestrator. We needed an issue tracker that works inside AI agent sessions. So we ported an open-source one to Rust and integrated it into the workflow. We needed to understand why some prompts waste tokens and others don't. So we built a prompt quality analyzer that extracts your messages from session logs, rates them, and shows you exactly where you're losing efficiency. A new AI model drops on OpenRouter — by the end of the week, someone on the team has tested it against our workflow and reported back. A new MCP server appears on GitHub — someone's already evaluated whether it solves a real problem for us. A new ---------- tool shows up on Twitter — someone's tried it in a real session. This isn't a scheduled R&D activity. It's how the team operates. The internal tools are mostly Rust and Go. The products are Flutter and TypeScript. Client work varies — we recently picked up a Drupal project, and the expectation was that the team could ramp on an unfamiliar framework in a day using AI-assisted exploration. That's the skill we hire for. What Makes This Team Different Every developer works alongside AI coding agents as core workflow — not as an experiment. You'll have: 5 AI coding runtimes at your workstation (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor) 30+ custom agent skills covering security, testing, architecture, code review, and prompt quality analysis Multi-agent coordination via MCP so you can run several AI assistants on different tasks simultaneously without file conflicts Automated quality gates (mutation testing, code metrics, security scanning, bug scanning) that give you confidence in AI-generated code before it hits review Prompt research tools that help you measure and improve how effectively you communicate with AI agents We don't just use these tools. We build them, research the protocols behind them, improve them, and expect every developer to have opinions about what works and what doesn't. What We Expect From You You experiment before you're told to. When a new AI model, CLI tool, MCP server, or workflow appears — on Twitter , Hacker News, a ---------- , wherever — your instinct is to install it and try it. Not bookmark it. Not wait for a tea ---------- eting. Try it, form a view, share what you found. You assess your own work. We have tools that analyze prompt quality, code review effectiveness, and development patterns. You're expected to run them on yourself, identify your own anti-patterns, and fix them. The existing setup is a starting point, not something to protect. Current numbers Right now: $92/day budget, ~6.87% conversion rate, ~NZ$76 CPA across two Search campaigns. Target is CPA under NZ$60 and conversion rate pushing toward 10%. Budget stays where it is until we can clearly see that more spend produces more quotes at a reasonable cost. Once we're there, that conversation happens quickly. The work Each week: Review search terms, add negatives, cut spend that isn't converting Adjust bids based on what's actually working Short email update: spend, conversions, CPA, what you changed and why Each month: Test ad copy — write new headlines, run them against current, cut the losers Review how budget is split across campaigns One-page summary: what moved, what didn't, what's next As needed: Propose new campaigns or restructures when you see an opportunity Flag wasted spend before it runs long Raise anything structural worth changing before the algorithm adapts to it If you think Facebook Ads or ---------- can drive more quotes cost-effectively, bring the proposal. If you have a view on whether those channels are worth revisiting, we want to hear it. How we work Email is the default. WhatsApp if something's urgent. A monthly call is available if you think it helps keep things aligned, but it's not required as long as the numbers are moving. You get full editor access. Day-to-day optimisation is yours to make. Anything that changes overall budget or campaign strategy needs a quick sign-off first. If you get the numbers moving, the scope grows with it. More campaigns, new channels, higher budget — that all gets scoped and paid separately. The base engagement is small by design. We grow it together once we can see the return. Familiarity with GA4 conversion tracking is a plus — we've had tracking issues in the past and want someone who notices that kind of thing early. title: AI-First Full-Stack Developer (Next.js)
description: # AI-First Full-Stack Developer (Next.js) — Moredemand (Remote) ## About Moredemand Moredemand is an AI-powered SaaS platform for paid advertising analytics, funnel building, and demand generation. We serve agency owners and in-house performance marketers who need to connect ad spend to revenue outcomes without the guesswork. The platform is in active build across multiple workstreams — ad account analytics, CRM and lead management, page and funnel builder, conversion mapping, and an AI assistant layer (MODA) that ties it all together. This is a ground-floor opportunity to shape a product that sits at the intersection of advertising data, automation, and applied AI. ## The Role We're hiring a full-stack developer whose default mode is building with AI — not just using it as a novelty feature, but treating it as core infrastructure. You'll be working across the Moredemand platform in Next.js, shipping features end-to-end from spec to production. This is a hands-on building role. You'll receive detailed specs and PRDs with user stories, business logic, and acceptance criteria (written in Gherkin). You won't be guessing what to build — but you will need to make smart technical decisions about how to build it, and move fast doing so. You'll be working alongside an existing small dev team and reporting directly to the founder. ## What You'll Be Doing - Building and shipping production features across the Moredemand platform in Next.js (App Router, Server Components, Server Actions) - Integrating AI/LLM capabilities throughout the product — not bolted-on chat widgets, but intelligent features woven into the user experience (triage, analysis, recommendations, natural language querying, content generation) - Working with the Google Ads, Meta Ads, and analytics APIs to ingest, normalise, and surface advertising data - Building CRM-style interfaces — database views, saved filters, inline actions, dynamic tables, drag-and-drop workflows - Developing the page/funnel builder module with overlay and popup elements - Implementing a consent management layer and data-triggered qualification rules - Writing clean, testable code against Gherkin acceptance criteria provided in each spec - Using Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent AI-assisted development tooling as a core part of your workflow — not occasionally, but as standard practice - Shipping iteratively with a bias toward working software over perfect abstractions ## What We're Looking For - Strong production experience with Next.js 14+ (App Router, not Pages Router) — this is non-negotiable - Proven ability to build with LLM APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar) — prompt engineering, structured outputs, tool use, streaming responses, RAG patterns - Comfortable across the full stack: React/TypeScript on the front end, Node.js/serverless on the back end, PostgreSQL or equivalent relational database - Experience integrating third-party APIs — particularly ad platforms, CRMs, or data-heavy SaaS integrations - Ability to work from a detailed spec and translate user stories and business logic into shipped features without requiring architectural hand-holding - Familiarity with AI-assisted development workflows (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, or similar) and the discipline to review and own what the tools produce - Test-driven mindset — you understand Gherkin acceptance criteria and write code that satisfies them - Clean component architecture, sensible state management, and an instinct for UI that feels fast and responsive - Self-directed and reliable in a remote, async-first environment — you ship, you communicate, you don't disappear ## Tech Environment - Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript - Tailwind CSS - PostgreSQL - Anthropic Claude API (primary LLM layer) - Google Ads API, Meta Marketing API - Vercel deployment - Claude Code / AI-assisted development as standard workflow - Spec-first methodology — block-based architecture, PRDs with Gherkin acceptance criteria, no code or DB schema in specs ## Bonus Points - Experience building SaaS platforms for marketers or agencies - Familiarity with advertising data models (campaigns, ad groups, keywords, conversion actions, attribution) - Experience with real-time dashboards, charting libraries (Recharts, D3), or data visualisation - Background in building form/page builders or drag-and-drop interfaces - Understanding of FCA-regulated or compliance-sensitive product environments - Contributions to open-source or a portfolio of shipped SaaS products ## How to Apply Send the following: 1. A short Loom (under 3 minutes) walking through a Next.js project you built — show the code, explain the decisions, highlight any AI/LLM integration 2. A brief description of how you currently use AI tooling in your development workflow — what tools, how often, and what you trust them with vs. what you don't 3. One example of a feature you shipped from spec to production, and what the spec looked like vs. what you delivered 4. Your availability (hours per week or full-time) and rate (hourly, daily, or monthly) No agencies. No CVs padded with frameworks you used once on a tutorial. Show the work.

title: Graphic Designer - Part Time (Remote)
description: The Compliance Services Organization didn’t exist. We built it. MP1 Solutions pioneered the Compliance Services Organization (CSO) — a new category of operating partner built to replace the fragmented vendor model that has defined compliance programs for decades. Built on the foundation of MedPro Disposal, the nation’s largest privately-held medical waste company serving 35,000+ providers across 48 states over the past 15 years, MP1 Solutions extends that operational infrastructure, vendor network, and customer trust into a category we’re actively building — and leading. What we do: We operate as the single compliance partner for non-acute healthcare facilities — consolidating every obligation into one coordinated program, assigning one dedicated account manager as the point of accountability, and actively managing the underlying vendor ecosystem through continuous evaluation, negotiation, and optimization on the practice’s behalf. Why it matters: Regulated facilities across the country are managing compliance the same fragmented way they always have. We’re changing that — and we’re looking for people who want to help build what comes next. Our technology: We’re actively building the AI infrastructure that sits behind this model — automating compliance tracking, surfacing risks before they become problems, and creating a system that gets smarter with every client we add. If you want to build at the intersection of compliance and technology, you’re in the right place. Our impact: Our clients never have to worry about something falling through the cracks — obligations are coordinated, tracked, and documented in one place. We audit costs, eliminate overcharges, and deliver proof of compliance that always keeps practices inspection ready. Position Overview: MedPro Disposal and MP1 Solutions compete in a market where first impressions are made visually — across paid ads, landing pages, sales collateral, and brand touchpoints that span two distinct but related brands. The Graphic Designer owns the visual execution layer for both, producing digital and print assets that are on-brand, conversion-focused, and built to perform in a high-volume marketing environment. This is not a passive production role. The right person brings creative instincts and design craft to every asset, understands how design decisions affect conversion and brand perception, and operates with enough independence to move fast without constant direction. Quality, consistency, and speed across two brands is the standard. Key Responsibilities: Digital Design: • Design high-converting paid ad creative for Google Display, Meta (Facebook /Instagram), and Reddit across both MedPro Disposal and MP1 Solutions — including static, carousel, and banner formats in all required platform dimensions. • Create landing page visual assets, hero images, icons, and supporting graphics that align with campaign objectives and brand standards. • Design social media graphics, email headers, and digital content assets for ongoing marketing programs across both brands. • Produce visual assets for web properties including comparison sites, client-facing tools, and web forms — in close coordination with the Web Developer. • Iterate quickly on creative variations for A/B testing — resizing, copy swaps, color variants, and format adaptations without sacrificing design quality. Print & Brand Collateral: • Design and produce print-ready sales collateral including one-pagers, brochures, sell sheets, and case study layouts for both brands. • Create branded presentation templates, pitch decks, and internal documents that maintain visual consistency across the organization. • Develop and maintain brand style elements — iconography, typography applications, color usage, and layout templates — that ensure consistency across all market-facing surfaces. • Support campaign launches with print materials, event graphics, and partner co-branded assets as needed. Brand Consistency & Creative Operations: • Maintain and enforce visual brand standards across both MedPro Disposal and MP1 Solutions — ensuring every asset, across every channel, looks like it belongs to the same professional organization. • Organize and maintain a shared asset library of approved brand elements, templates, and production files that the broader team can access and use. • Collaborate with the Paid Media Manager, SEO & AEO Specialist, and Web Developer to ensure design assets are correctly sized, formatted, and optimized for their intended platform and purpose. • Manage multiple concurrent design requests through Asana, prioritizing effectively and communicating proactively when timelines are at risk. Qualifications: Required: • 3+ years of graphic design experience with a strong portfolio demonstrating both digital and print work — portfolio submission is required and will be the primary evaluation criteria. • Expert-level proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite — specifically Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign. This is non-negotiable; candidates must demonstrate mastery, not familiarity. • Proven experience designing paid digital ad creative across Google Display, Meta, and similar platforms — with an understanding of what makes ad creative perform, not just look good. • Solid print design experience: bleed setup, CMYK color management, print-ready file preparation, and working with print production specifications. • Strong typography skills and a sharp eye for layout, hierarchy, and visual balance across both digital and print formats. • Experience maintaining brand consistency across multiple brands or product lines simultaneously. • Asana or equivalent project management tool experience — able to self-manage a queue of concurrent design requests without micromanagement. • High proficiency with AI design tools (Adobe Firefly, Midjourney, or equivalent) for concept generation, image enhancement, and accelerating production workflows. We expect AI to be a standard part of how this person works. • Excellent written English for creative briefs, revision requests, and cross-team communication. • Must be available to overlap with U.S. Central Standard Time (CST) business hours for collaboration and feedback cycles. Nice-to-Have: • Experience with Figma or similar tools for web-adjacent design work and handoff to developers. • Motion graphics or basic video editing capability (After Effects, Premiere, or Canva Pro) for social and ad content. • Experience designing for healthcare, B2B SaaS, or compliance-driven brands. • Canva Pro proficiency for rapid template creation and lightweight asset production. • Experience working with U.S.-based marketing teams remotely, with strong cross-cultural communication skills. Compensation & Benefits: • Competitive hourly rate of $5–$8/hour USD, based on experience and portfolio strength • Part-time role (20 hours/week) with flexible scheduling and weekly pay • 100% remote work — work from anywhere in the Philippines • Long-term engagement with growth potential within a U.S.-based organization • Collaborative and performance-driven culture focused on professional development and results • Exposure to U.S. marketing operations, brand strategy, and multi-brand creative environments • Opportunity to grow your portfolio working across paid media, print, and digital channels Technical Requirements: • Personal laptop or desktop capable of running Adobe Creative Suite without lag • Stable primary internet connection (at least 25–30 Mbps) with a backup internet source • Quiet, dedicated work environment Application Process: To apply, please submit the following: 1. Your most updated resume; 2. Send it to these email address: ---------- and ---------- 3. Portfolio link or attached samples showcasing digital ad creative, print collateral, and brand work 4. Brief introduction about your experience and why you’re a fit for this role Portfolio submissions without a portfolio will not be reviewed. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. MedPro Disposal and MP1 Solutions are equal opportunity employers. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Excellent attention to detail. Ability to solve problems and use initiative. Experience with Airbnb, ---------- or serviced accommodation is beneficial but not essential. Communication & Equipment Requirements To be considered for this position, you must have: A stable and reliable high-speed internet connection. A smartphone or telephone capable of making and receiving calls. A laptop or desktop computer suitable for managing bookings and communications. Availability to respond to urgent guest enquiries when required. A quiet and professional working environment. You will be expected to communicate with guests, cleaners, contractors and company partners in a professional and friendly manner at all times. Performance Bonuses5-Star Review Bonus Receive a bonus for every five 5-star reviews received across our properties. Response Time Bonus Receive bonuses for maintaining excellent guest response times. Initiative Bonus Additional bonuses will be awarded when initiative is shown and problems are solved without requiring constant supervision. Growth Bonus As the company grows, additional responsibilities and pay increases will become available. Commission StructureLong-Term Booking Commission You will receive: 10% commission on any long-term booking that you personally secure through your outreach efforts. This includes bookings from: Insurance accommodation providers Insurance companies Contractors Corporate clients Relocation companies Local businesses This commission is paid in addition to your monthly salary and performance bonuses. Additional Work Bonus At Jules Comfort Stays, we believe in rewarding hard work and initiative. In addition to your salary, commission and performance bonuses, you will receive additional bonuses for: Taking on extra responsibilities. Completing work outside of your normal duties. Assisting with special projects. Helping onboard new properties. Creating new systems or improving existing processes. Successfully solving difficult guest or operational issues. Supporting the growth and expansion of the business. Assisting with marketing and social media content. Helping source new contractors, suppliers or business opportunities. We value tea ---------- mbers who go above and beyond. If you consistently demonstrate reliability, initiative and a positive attitude, there will be opportunities for increased earnings, promotions and greater responsibility within the company. Career Progression This role has the potential to grow into: Senior Virtual Assistant Operations Manager Property Manager Business Development Manager As Jules Comfort Stays continues to expand, we are committed to rewarding loyal tea ---------- mbers who contribute to the company's success. title: SEO Content QA Specialist (VA) — Remote
description: I run a small, established SEO agency for local businesses in Australia, and I'm looking for someone with a sharp eye to join me on a project basis to start, with a clear path to something long-term for the right person. THE ROLE Our content process is heavily AI-assisted. That means the role isn't writing from a blank page, it's quality control: taking AI-generated content and making it genuinely client-ready. Here's the core of it: your job is to make everything perfect before it reaches me. I'm the final glance, not the proofreader. By the time work lands on my desk, it should already be right, polished, accurate, client-ready. Nothing obviously off, nothing half-checked. Day to day, that means: - Proofreading and editing AI-written content to a high standard - Tailoring content so it actually fits each client, not just generic output 9You'll be responsible for intimately understanding each business we work with and tailor content for them) - Checking SEO keyword inclusions read naturally and aren't forced or janky - Preparing client-facing report documents that require careful, accurate editing - Some Google business Profile work This is detail work, and the detail is the deliverable. The single most important trait is a keen eye: catching the things that are obviously off and self-checking your own work before you hand it over, every time. WHO THIS IS FOR - You have a background in copywriting and understand what good SEO-optimised content looks like - You're comfortable using AI tools day to day (we use Claude heavily, including Claude skills, so genuine confidence here matters) - You're tech-comfortable and can follow a process without needing hand-holding on every step - You work autonomously. I hire people because they're skilled enough to do the work on their own. We have training and SOPs for exactly that reason. - You know when to reach out if something's unclear, rather than handing in work that misses the mark THE SETUP - Fully remote, with genuine freedom over when you work. Time is tracked, but you're not clocking in and out to set hours. It's self-paced - A lot of trust is placed on you to do high-quality work independently - This starts as a single project and will likely be intensive up front. If it goes well, I'll be inviting you to stay on, first part-time, then into a well-paid full-time position If you're someone looking to prove yourself and earn a great long-term role, this is that opportunity.
