title: Cold Email Specialist (Infrastructure + Copy + Deliverability, Full Stack) - Long-Term
job_title: Cold Email Specialist (Infrastructure + Copy + Deliverability, Full Stack) - Long-Term
description: Compensation: $600 to $1,000 USD per month based on what you can prove. Hours: 40 hours per week. Some overlap with Morocco, Dubai, and EU business hours required (Manila 3 PM to 11 PM works for us; flexible within that range). READ THIS FIRST This is not an entry-level role. We are not looking for someone who watched a "cold email in 2026" YouTube playlist and sent 200 email s from their Gmail. We are looking for someone who has built sending infrastructure from zero, run real campaigns at volume, kept domains healthy, and booked real meetings for a real business. If that's not you yet, this isn't your post. If your experience is "I wrote cold email copy for a client once" or "I managed a VA team that did outreach", stop reading. The tests will expose it in an hour. ABOUT RMD RMD is a digital marketing agency. Our team is distributed across Morocco and Dubai and works remote. Our primary client base is in Dubai and the GCC, with growing work across the EU and North Africa. We run SEO, paid ads, branding, and web development for service businesses, e-commerce stores, and B2B companies in 20+ countries. WHAT THIS ROLE IS You own our outbound email machine end to end. Not just the copy. Not just the sending tool. The whole stack: 1. Infrastructure: secondary domains, mailboxes, DNS, warmup, sending health 2. Data: sourcing lead lists, cleaning them, verifying them, segmenting them 3. Copy: short plain-text sequences that get replies, not opens 4. Operations: campaign builds, launch checklists, inbox management, meeting booking, weekly reporting We already run a multi-domain, multi-mailbox sending setup on Instantly with a live campaign program into the GCC. You will take it over, keep it healthy, and scale it: first for RMD's own client acquisition, then for client campaigns as we grow the service. If you only want to write copy and hand the "technical stuff" to someone else, this role isn't a fit. The technical stuff IS the role. Copy that never lands in the inbox is decoration. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Set up and maintain sending infrastructure: buy secondary domains, configure SPF / DKIM / DMARC, create mailboxes, set custom tracking domains, run warmup, monitor health scores - Source lead lists by niche, title, and country (Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator + scraper, LeadRocks, or equivalent), with GCC and EU targeting - Clean and verify every list before upload: strip free email domains, dedupe, verify (Reoon, MillionVerifier, or equivalent), enrich missing fields, make the catch-all keep-or-cut call - Write 3-step plain-text sequences (opener, bump, breakup) with personalization variables that actually render, and iterate them on reply-rate data - Build and launch campaigns in Instantly: schedules in the prospect's timezone and work week (much of the GCC runs Sunday to Thursday, the UAE runs Monday to Friday), stop-on-reply, text-only, daily caps per mailbox, domain-clustering caps per recipient company - Diagnose deliverability problems before they kill a domain: bounce spikes, spam placement, blacklists, when to pause vs rotate vs retire a mailbox - Manage the reply inbox daily: triage, answer objections, push for the meeting, book it on the calendar, hand the warm lead to the CEO with context - Report weekly with the numbers that matter: delivered, reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings booked per 1,000 sends, infra health - Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude) as part of the daily workflow. AI is openly used in the agency, not as a shortcut to skip thinking - Communicate with the team in writing daily (email , ClickUp). Updates short, blockers raised early REQUIRED (WE WILL VERIFY ALL OF THIS) - 2+ years running cold email campaigns end to end. Sourcing to inbox to booked meeting. Not "I wrote sequences". Ran the machine. - 2 campaigns from the last 12 months you can walk through with numbers: niche, list size, total sends, reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings or sales calls booked. With platform screenshots (redact client names if NDA). We will dig into these on the test and the call. - You have built sending infrastructure from zero, yourself. Domains bought, DNS records configured (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), mailboxes created on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, warmup run, custom tracking domain set. Be ready to explain each DNS record's job in plain words. - Instantly in production. Smartlead or lemlist accepted if you can map over fast, but you should know your way around a sending platform's campaign builder, schedules, account health, and code/variable view without a tutorial. - One deliverability save you can tell start to finish. A domain or mailbox that started burning (bounces, spam folder, health drop), what you checked, what the root cause was, what fixed it, and what the numbers did after. "I just slowed the sending" is not a save story. - List building in production. You have pulled targeted B2B lists by title + industry + country from Apollo, Sales Navigator + a scraper, LeadRocks, or equivalent, and you know why a narrow GCC query returns 9 results while the same query in the US returns 9,000. - Email verification workflow. You verify every list before upload, you know the difference between valid, invalid, catch-all, and unknown, and you can defend when a catch-all is worth the bounce risk. - Copy that gets replies. Short, plain text, one idea per email , specific CTA, follow-ups that bump instead of re-pitching. You can name your benchmark reply rate by market and what you change first when a campaign comes in under it. - Reply handling to booked meetings. You have personally worked an outbound inbox: objections, "send me more info", ghosting, and you have booked meetings from it. Outbound that ends at "positive reply" is half a job. - Cold email canon. You have studied at least 2 of: Nick Saraev, Alex Hormozi ($100M Leads, the outreach chapters), Eric Nowoslawski, Daniel Fazio, Jay Feldman. Name a principle from one of them and point to a campaign above where you used it. - English fluency at C1 or higher. Your email s read like a human wrote them, not a template engine. - Stable internet, quiet workspace, 40 hours per week available. If we struggle to find the profile at this exact bar, we may relax the experience minimum case-by-case. We will not relax the campaign-numbers + infrastructure + deliverability evidence floor. BONUS (NOT REQUIRED) - Clay (enrichment workflows, waterfall verification) - Google Postmaster Tools and inbox placement testing in production - B2B experience in GCC, EU, or US markets specifically - French (we have France and North Africa clients) - Light automation (Zapier, Make) for lead routing and reporting - LinkedIn outreach experience alongside email (multichannel sequencing) WHO WE HIRE - People who ship the work and don't disappear - People who want a long-term role, not a gig - People who can take direction in writing, push back when they think we're wrong, and own a deliverable end to end - People who can show their work, not just describe it WHAT WE OFFER - $600 to $1,000 USD per month based on what you can prove. L2 tunneling, anycast gateways, VLANs, trunk/access ports, LACP/LAG, IRB/SVI, and L2/L3 troubleshooting. Read, write, review, and safely apply Juniper set-style config. Strong IPv4/IPv6 subnetting. Troubleshooting with ping, traceroute, MTR, tcpdump, interface counters, route tables, logs, and looking-glass tools. Understand customer impact before making changes; work independently with sound judgment. Strong written English for customer updates, internal notes, and escalation summaries. ISP / hosting / data center / NOC / service-provider background strongly preferred. Preferred Skills Cisco Nexus platforms. Transit providers, IXes, route servers, peering, IRR, RPKI/ROA, AS-SETs, LOA validation. Monitoring: PRTG, LibreNMS, Prometheus, Grafana, or similar. Automation/documentation: NetBox, Git, Oxidized, Ansible, Python. DDoS response, RTBH, traffic engineering, carrier escalations. Linux networking and server-side troubleshooting. You are having a simple conversation: their current policy costs more and offers less — we can switch them to a better carrier with lower premiums and added benefits. title: Product Manager
description: What you'll own Each of our clients is an AI consumer company trying to turn a launch into pipeline. Your job is to own one of those launches end-to-end - we call this a play. A play is a 6-8 week campaign: you pick the creators, write the brief, ship the content, watch the metrics, kill what's not working, double down on what is. Most plays drive 50K-500K installs or signups for the AI product. You are the single throat to choke for one product's launch. You own the outcome. What you'll actually do Define the launch hypothesis. What's the user behavior change this product is betting on? Who's the early adopter? What's the hook that gets them in the door? Source creators. You find your own creators - 10-30 per week in the product's niche across TikTok, IG, and YouTube Shorts. We give you the sourcing tools, the existing creator database (50K+), and the criteria. There is no separate sourcer; the play is yours end-to-end. Brief and ship. Write the creative brief, send the assignments, answer creator questions in our shared Slack channels. Get content out the door fast. Measure and iterate. Track posts, views, conversions. Run experiments on hook, format, and CTA. Weekly decisions on what to kill and what to scale. Report. Weekly written update on the play: what shipped, what we learned, what's next. Direct dialogue with the client founder. Who this is for This page exists because we believe great operators get priced out of the global tech market for reasons that have nothing to do with their ability. We want to find them and pay them fairly for the value they create, while building the most diverse and capable PM team in creator marketing. Self-taught is welcome. We do not care about which university you went to or any school credential. Show us what you've shipped and what you watch and how you think. Ships things. You have launched something. A TikTok account, a Shopify store, a Discord community, a Substack, a side product. Anything where you had to make 100 small decisions and learn from outcomes. Lives on short-form video. You can name 5 creator accounts you follow in different niches and explain exactly why each one works. Bonus if some are South East Asian creators - we want that local context. AI-native. You don't just use ChatGPT. You build small things with Claude, Cursor, v0, Lovable, ElevenLabs, Runway. Whatever the job needs. Comfortable with async + overlap hours. Most work is on your own schedule, but you can do 2-4 hours of US or EU overlap a few times a week for client calls. What you have shipped matters more than any school you went to. What you'll get Paid in USD. $400-$600/month base depending on hours and experience, plus performance bonus tied to your play's outcomes. The bonus can be larger than the base for top performers, paid in USD via Wise or Payoneer. Real ownership. You own one product's launch, then 2-3 as you ramp. Your name on the work, directly visible to the founders of the AI products we're launching. The 8x playbook. Every internal SOP, every creator network, every tool. We hand you what took 18 months to build. Direct path to extend. 3-month role to start. Top performers extend or convert to permanent roles at increased comp. Mentorship from the team. Weekly 1:1 with the head of plays. Direct line to the CEO when you need it. The same operating context the EU team gets. $3M+ Run rate 100k+ Creators in network 30+ Countries About 8x Social 8x Social is the infrastructure layer for performance-driven creator marketing. We work with the fastest-growing AI consumer companies to turn their launches into pipeline, connecting them with 100k+ creators across 30+ countries. Founded by Jaka Bavdek (CEO, London Business School) and Theo Bui (CTO, Imperial College), we're backed by Entrepreneur First and based in San Francisco. We're the fastest-growing company in EF history. We are explicitly building a globally distributed PM team because we believe talent is everywhere even when opportunity isn't. If you want to operate on real AI launches with full ownership, this is the most direct way in.

We are aiming for approximately 5–9 published content touchpoints per day across all platforms. This does not mean 9 completely unique posts every day. We expect smart repurposing across platforms. For example, a single educational topic may become: * 1 Instagram carousel * 1 Facebook post * 1 X thread or several short X posts * 1 TikTok/Reel/Short * 3–5 Instagram/Facebook stories ## Weekly Minimum Deliverables At minimum, we would like help producing: * 5–7 Instagram main posts per week * 20–35 Instagram/Facebook stories per week * 5–7 Facebook posts per week * 3–5 TikToks/Reels/YouTube Shorts per week to start * 15–25 X posts per week * 3–5 YouTube Shorts per week * 1 weekly content calendar * 1 weekly performance summary * 10–20 new content ideas for future posts As we create more video content with our provider, we would like to increase short-form video production. ## Content Topics Content will focus on topics such as: * Anxiety * Depression * ADHD * Medication management * Telehealth psychiatry * Mental health education * What to expect as a new patient * Psychiatry myths * Therapy vs psychiatry * Self-care and coping skills * Appointment availability * Local New Jersey mental health content * Patient FAQs ## Important Healthcare Content Rules Because this is a healthcare practice, content must be professional, ethical, and compliant. description: * YOU MUST SPEAK FLUENT ENGLISH * We're a US-based virtual real estate company looking for a detail-oriented Data Manager to run our daily lead pipeline. Every morning you'll pull fresh distress lists from county sources, scrub the data, run skip tracing and phone verification, then import clean, dial-ready leads into our CRM before our acquisitions team starts calling. The work is consistent, structured, and rewards accuracy. If you're the kind of person who notices a misspelled column header and fixes it without being asked — keep reading. This is a long-term role. We want someone who will own this pipeline for years, not weeks. Schedule - Hours: 40 hours per week - Days: Monday through Friday - Time zone: 9am-6pm (CST) - Deadline: All daily lists must be live in our CRM daily. Pay - $4–6 USD/hour depending on experience - Paid bi-weekly via Payoneer or PayPal - Performance bonus for clean data quality and on-time delivery - Raise review at 90 days What You'll Do Every Day: 1. Pull distress lists from county government portals: probate, auction, tax delinquent, pre-foreclosure, and auction. 2. Scrub the data in Google Sheets — dedupe by APN, standardize addresses to USPS format, remove vacant land, cross-check against our CRM. 3. Organize each list into our standard 14-column upload format 4. Run the cleaned list through BatchLeads for skip tracing 5. Verify every phone number through Trestle (activity score, line type, connection status) 6. Reorder phones so the highest-scored number lands in Phone 1 7. Import the final file into FreedomSoft with the correct campaign tag and pipeline stage 8. Log every step in our Master Tracker (raw count, scrubbed count, hit rate, etc.) A full Standard Operating Procedure with screenshots and a worked example will be provided. You will not be figuring this out from scratch. Tools You'll Use: - Google Sheets (heavy daily use — formulas, filters, dedupe, VLOOKUP) - FreedomSoft (our CRM — we'll train you) - XLeads (skip tracing) - Trestle (phone verification) - County government websites (varies by list type) - Slack (daily check-ins and questions) What We Need From You: - Strong Google Sheets skills — you should be comfortable with formulas, filters, dedupe, and conditional formatting - Sharp attention to detail — bad data costs us real money - Comfortable navigating unfamiliar government websites and exporting CSVs - Reliable high-speed internet and a quiet workspace - Good written English for daily Slack updates - Available Mon–Fri without exception (this is a daily pipeline — one missed day backs up the whole team) - Able to start As Soon As Possible Bonus Points If You Have: - Prior US real estate experience - Experience with FreedomSoft, BatchLeads, PropStream, or any real estate CRM - Background in data entry, list management, or data cleaning roles - Skip tracing experience (Xleads, Skip Genie, IDI, TLO, etc.) - Familiarity with US county records systems What Makes This Role Different: - Structured, repeatable work. This is not a "wear many hats" VA role. You'll do the same workflow every day and get faster at it every week. - Clear ownership. You own the pipeline. Your numbers (hit rate, dead phone rate, on-time delivery) are visible to the team every Friday. - Long-term growth. As we scale, you'll have the chance to train other VAs on this workflow and move into a team lead role. You won't be making cold calls. This is back-office data work. We have a separate Acquisitions Team for outreach. How to Apply 1. Include the word PIPELINE at the top of your application. Applications without this word will be deleted unread. 2. title: Virtual Assistant - Travel Concierge
description: We're looking for a **Travel Concierge** who is passionate about crafting seamless travel experiences and delivering high-quality client service. This role is for someone who loves travel, writes with warmth and clarity, thinks fast when plans change, and takes pride in the kind of attention to detail that makes clients feel like VIPs from the first message through check-in. ## Why You'll Want to Join - You will be paid in **USD** (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th) - **Paid Time Off** in accordance with company policy - Observance of **Holidays** per company guidelines - **100% remote setup** so you can work wherever you're most productive - Your updated resume highlighting any customer service or travel-related experience 2. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself and sharing why you are passionate about travel and client service 3. A short writing sample such as an email , WhatsApp message, or short paragraph showing your conversational tone Only candidates who submit a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process. title: Company Accountant

invoice processing, cash application, collections, and supplier reconciliations • Reconcile bank accounts daily in Odoo, independent of the payments you process • Perform monthly inventory reconciliation — reconcile the inventory subledger to the GL and investigate all stock variances • Process payroll for all employees in Rippling — prepare, reconcile, and submit for written approval before any funding • Prepare BAS workpapers and coordinate with the external accountant for lodgement • Meet all Australian statutory obligations — PAYG withholding, superannuation, and payroll tax on time • Prepare monthly P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement with variance commentary for management • Assist management with weekly cash flow forecasting and working capital monitoring • Maintain Odoo chart of accounts integrity and document all finance processes as SOPs What We Are Looking For • Degree in Accounting or Finance — CPA or equivalent preferred • Minimum 4 years accounting experience with at least 2 years owning a finance function end-to-end • Strong, hands-on Odoo experience across finance modules — able to work independently without system support • Experience in a business holding physical inventory — essential • Experience with inventory reconciliation and stock management in Odoo or a comparable ERP — essential • Solid knowledge of Australian GST, BAS, PAYG withholding, and payroll tax obligations • Experience with Rippling payroll or an equivalent cloud payroll platform • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets — reconciliation workpapers and financial reporting • Strong written English — able to report clearly to Australian management • Self-directed and reliable — genuinely comfortable as the sole finance resource What We Offer • Full ownership of a finance function — genuine responsibility, not a support role • Stable, long-term contractor engagement • Direct access to the business operations lead and group CFO • A small, focused business where your work makes an immediate and visible difference This is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of a finance function and work directly with business leaders in a growing Australian trade services business. title: Personal Assistant (in-person / requires travel)
description: My name is Scott Watkins and I am the owner of a small software development company.  And while we are based in the United States, most of our workforce is in the Philippines. Actually, our company was one of the first to use the OnlineJobs.ph platform, and John (owner of OnlineJobs) was the one who actually sold us on using the platform.  Today, our small company hires all our staff solely from OnlineJobs.Ph Here is a brief interview from OnlineJobs showcasing our company: ---------- ================================== JOB DESRIPTION So, my wife (Filipina) and I regularly travel to the Philippines to visit her family and collaborate with our VAs/Staff. We will be arriving in the Philippines this coming late August, and will stay through the first three weeks of September. I am looking to hire someone who can assist me in researching and planning my itinerary before we arrive (so will technically be my VA before arriving).  They will then meet us upon arrival and will act as my Personal Assistant for the duration of our stay.  Then after we leave, they will follow-up with closing out and finishing any unfinished business left there. The job will pay an hourly rate based on the number of hours available and worked prior to our arrival .. then will pay a flat rate for the duration of our stay there, followed by an indeterminate amount after we leave based on the work required. For the most part, while there, the PA will go wherever I go and spend everyday with me.  They will be given time each day for themselves of-course, but will need to be flexible depending on circumstances.  We will be bringing our children, so there will also be some days dedicated to spending time with the family (e.g. Enchanted Kingdom, etc). There will be some days that my wife and I may plan to leave the kids behind and visit certain places as well (e.g. Floating Restaurant in Bohol, etc).  Other times, my wife may wish to go off into the province and visit her relatives (which I definitely do not like doing), so I may d ---------- to travel by myself to exotic locations around the Philippines, play golf, or just hit up the local malls.  Due to the time difference, I also tend to be a night owl there, and enjoy hitting up clubs/bars/KTVs for some nightly entertainment. There are too many things to list out, but regardless of where we go and what I do, the PA's job will be to always make sure to be by my side, ensure that I make it safely to whatever destination we go, ensure I have a fun and enjoyable time, and ensure I always return home safely.  This may include running small errands (e.g. getting food/medicine) and occasionally traveling by themselves (e.g. meeting a venue owner to finalize details). But 95% of the time they will be at my side. There are other things that may be involved (e.g. lodging arrangements and travel accommodations) that will also be discussed in the interview. But I will cover all expenses for everything; including food, accommodations, travel, and personal expenses.  Including also the salary, which will be discussed and d ---------- based on skills, experience, and meeting requirements. Previous experience is not necessary. The main things that matter the most are: - Understand/Speak English for long periods of time - Honesty and Loyalty to me - Willing to go where I want to go, do what I want to do, and ensure I enjoy myself going/doing it - A consistently positive attitude and eager to please - An adventurous spirit and willing to go places and do things never done before - Being flexible and adaptable as things change (as they always do in the Philippines) - Willing to put in the work and effort to ensure we have a great and smooth vacation People who are naturally open and conversational will also have a great advantage (e.g. Westerners love to socialize) All are welcome to apply no matter the location, gender, age, religion, or marital status.  I have hired them all in previous trips.  However, in my previous experience, Younger PAs tend to be more adventurous, Filipinas tend to speak better English, and married individuals tend to be more 'intuitive' with my and my family needs. Additionally, my wife is from Davao, so Bisaya/Cebuano will give you an advantage with her, though not required for me. - But I am open to considering any and all who wish to apply. If you think you might enjoy traveling the country, accompanying one of the world's greatest bosses, and visiting some of the nicest places the Philippines has to offer, all at my expense ... then I invite you to click on the link and fill out our short application form here: ---------- You may also email me at ---------- - be sure to include your OnlineJobs profile link, FB, and WhatsApp. Though filling out the online application will get better response times. Our Stack (you'll work across most of this) -Zapier (advanced: code steps, webhooks, paths, error handling — not just simple Zaps) -Airtable (automations, scripting, complex base design, API) -Pipedrive CRM (API, webhooks, workflow automation) -ActiveCampaign (automations, API) -Python (Flask services deployed on Google Cloud Run) -REST APIs generally — reading API docs and building reliable integrations is the core of this job -LLM integrations (Claude / OpenAI APIs — building automations that use AI models via API) -WordPress — custom code (PHP/HTML/CSS/JS), performance optimisation (Core Web Vitals), and ongoing site management. Not just themes and plugins — you must be able to work in the code. -Google Tag Manager & tracking — GTM container setup, dataLayer coding, UTM parameter architecture, conversion tracking (including server-side / Conversions API) -Cloudflare, DNS, domains & hosting — DNS records, security settings, SSL, domain management (GoDaddy etc.), hosting environments -Softr (client portal on top of Airtable) -Plus: SMS APIs (Twilio/Sinch), Meta Conversions API, and AI voice APIs You don't need experience with every tool — but you MUST be strong on Zapier + Airtable + APIs + Python + WordPress (real coding, not just plugins), and able to learn the rest fast from documentation. What You'll Do -Build new automations and improve existing ones (lead routing, CRM workflows, client notifications, and LLM-powered automation systems) -Own our WordPress website end-to-end: performance (Core Web Vitals), custom code changes, design polish, and reliability -Own our tracking infrastructure: GTM, dataLayer, UTM architecture, and conversion tracking accuracy across Meta and Google -Manage the infrastructure layer: Cloudflare, DNS, domains, hosting, SSL, and security settings -Innovate with AI. We use LLMs heavily across our systems and expect you to stay current with new models, tools, and techniques — and to proactively propose where AI can improve or replace existing processes. "I saw this new capability and built a prototype" is the energy we pay bonuses for. -Debug production issues by finding root causes — not patching symptoms -Integrate third-party APIs by reading official documentation carefully and verifying exact parameter specs (this is a hard requirement for us — guessing at API parameters is how systems break) -Write clear documentation: every automation you ship comes with a written spec and runbook. No exceptions. -Proactively identify problems and improvements before being asked — we pay bonuses specifically for this Compensation -Base: USD $2,500–3,000/month depending on experience -Monthly performance bonus: USD $300–800 based on shipped systems that run reliably, documentation quality, and -proactive problem-finding. Opportunity to go even higher, based on performance. -Annual base increases for strong performers -Long-term, stable, full-time role — we are building for years, not months Hours Of Work Full-time, Monday–Friday, working - 9am - 6pm SYDNEY TIME. Who This Role Suits -5+ years building automations, integrations, and websites professionally — you're a senior generalist who's comfortable owning the entire technical surface of a business, not a specialist in one tool -You're a problem solver and have a high degree of attention to detail -You chase root causes, not symptoms — "I found why it breaks" instead of "I added a workaround" -You read API documentation for fun (or at least without pain) -You're genuinely excited by AI — you already use LLMs in your own workflow, follow new releases, and have built things with -AI APIs because you wanted to, not just because a client asked -You test your own work before calling it done -You communicate clearly and proactively — if something is blocked or broken, we hear it from you first -You want one stable long-term client who pays well and pays bonuses, not five gigs Who This Role Does NOT Suit -Anyone whose Zapier experience is limited to simple two-step Zaps -Anyone whose WordPress experience is page builders only (Elementor/Divi) — if you can't work directly in PHP/HTML/CSS/JS and diagnose performance issues in the code, this isn't your role -Anyone who hardcodes credentials or guesses at API parameters instead of checking docs -Anyone juggling multiple clients (we require exclusivity during work hours) -Agencies, teams, or anyone planning to subcontract any part of this work. We are hiring you, one individual — the person we interview is the person who does the work, always. Given the financial data our systems handle, subcontracting is treated as a serious breach and grounds for immediate termination. -Anyone uncomfortable with logged/audited system access — we run strict security practices (scoped credentials, audit trails). Honest builders find this boring; that's the point. Security Note (read this — it matters) We work with financial data, so we follow least-privilege access practices: you'll use your own named accounts and scoped API keys, production credentials are managed by the owner, and system activity is logged. This is standard, professional, and protects you as much as us. If that sounds reasonable, we'll get along great. SKILL REQUIREMENTS Required: -Zapier (Expert) -Airtable (Expert) -AI Tool Use — Claude Code / ChatGPT (Expert) -API Integration / REST APIs (Expert) -WordPress — custom code & performance (Advanced) -Google Tag Manager / UTM / conversion tracking (Advanced) -Python (Advanced) -HTML / CSS / JavaScript (Advanced) -Webhooks (Advanced) -Cloudflare / DNS / domain & hosting management (Intermediate–Advanced) Strongly preferred: -Pipedrive or similar CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce) -ActiveCampaign or similar (Mailchimp, Klaviyo) -Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions) -Flask or similar Python web frameworks -Meta Conversions API / server-side tracking Nice to have: -Softr / no-code app builders -Twilio / Sinch / Kixie, SMS APIs -SQL HOW TO APPLY To apply, send a message that includes ALL of the following — applications missing any item will not be read: 1. Start your message with the word "PINEAPPLE" so we know you read the full post. 2. Your 2–3 best automation/integration projects — for each: what it did, which tools/APIs were involved, and one problem you hit and how you solved it. Specific detail matters more than polish. Include links wherever possible — live websites you've built or optimised, GitHub, portfolio, or Loom walkthroughs. Claims we can verify are worth far more than claims we can't. 3. Answer this question: A Zapier webhook step is receiving data from a third-party API, but one field arrives blank for about 4% of records even though the source system shows the data exists. Describe, step by step, how you would diagnose this. (There is no single right answer — we're looking at how you think.) 4. Answer this question: A WordPress landing page scores poorly on Core Web Vitals (high CLS, slow LCP) and its Meta conversion tracking is undercounting leads. Briefly: what are the first things you'd check for each problem? 5. Your expected monthly salary in USD. 6. Confirm you can work 9:00am–6:00pm Sydney time (including the earlier Manila start during Australian daylight saving) full-time and exclusively. 7. A short video introduction (3–5 minutes, camera on) — Loom or similar. Briefly: who you are, what you've built that you're proudest of, and what specifically about this role appeals to you. No script needed, no editing, no polish — we just want to meet the actual person we'd be talking to every morning. If you're selected, we'll contact you back to arrange a quick interview to see if we're a good fit to work together.

title: Product Researcher for Google Ads
description: About us We run a portfolio of e-commerce webshops powered by Google Ads. Each store carries thousands of products, and we add hundreds of new ones every single week. Our edge is speed and selection: we find products people are already searching for on Google, list them fast, and let demand do the rest. We sell primarily into the German market (DACH region), so a deep, instinctive feel for what German consumers want — and what they'll want next — is the heart of this role. The role We're looking for an experienced Product Researcher who can consistently spot products that will trend in the coming months before they peak — and validate that real Google search demand exists behind them. You'll feed our pipeline with a steady, high-quality stream of products that have proven search volume and rising interest in Germany. This is a research-and-judgment role, not a data-entry role. We need someone whose product picks reliably convert into search traffic and sales. What you'll do - Research and identify products with rising or established Google search demand in the German/DACH market. - Forecast upcoming trends and seasonal demand 1–6 months ahead, and flag products before they saturate. - Validate demand using tools like Google Keyword Planner, Google Trends, ---------- , and search volume / keyword data. - Deliver a weekly shortlist of vetted products (target: hundreds per week across stores) with search volume, seasonality, and competition notes. - Track competitors, marketplaces ( ---------- , Otto, Kaufland, ---------- ), and German social/shopping trends. - Work closely with our Google Ads and listing teams so winning products get to market fast. What you bring - Proven track record in e-commerce product research, trend spotting, or dropshipping/retail sourcing — with results you can point to. - Deep knowledge of the German market: consumer behaviour, seasonality, language nuances, and what sells in DACH. - Hands-on skill with Google Keyword Planner, Google Trends, and search-volume tools; comfortable reading keyword and demand data. - An eye for timing — you understand the difference between a fad, a trend, and an evergreen. - High output without sacrificing quality; you can work at the pace of "hundreds of products a week." - Self-directed, data-driven, and comfortable in a fast-moving remote team. Nice to have - Experience with Google Ads / Shopping campaigns. - Familiarity with Shopify or similar platforms. - Knowledge of German marketplace ecosystems and import/sourcing channels. How to apply Send us: - A short note on your product-research experience and the German market. - 3 products you believe will trend in DACH over the next 3 months — with the Google search data that backs your pick. Your availability and rate/salary expectation. The 3-product test is the part we read first. Show us how you think.

Customer service experience is a plus, not a requirement. We'd rather hire a kind, hungry learner with zero call experience than an experienced agent who runs a script. If your English is clear and neutral and you truly love helping people and dogs, we'll teach you the rest. We're a small pet supplement company. Our customers are devoted dog parents. Their dogs are all ages, some healthy, some dealing with health issues, and they reach out to us by email , text, and phone for help. We have a strong in-house knowledge base, and we'll train you on it thoroughly before you ever speak with a customer. This is not a call center job If your training is to apologize warmly and move on to the next call, this role will frustrate you. We never measure call times. We measure whether the customer got real help. Being sweet on the phone is the baseline here. The job is getting the customer a real answer. We're a small, personable business where each customer gets dedicated, white-glove care. You'll have time to actually listen, and to remember a customer's dog's name from her last call. Every email and every call gets treated like it matters. Before you take calls alone, we'll train you for weeks on our products and our head herbalist's teaching, and you'll pass a product knowledge check in your first 30 days. When a dog mom asks how other customers get a picky senior dog to take her herbs, we expect an answer from that training. When you don't know, the answer is "I'll find out and call you back today." Then you find out, and you call back. Part of the job is knowing the line: ordering and product questions you handle yourself, deeper health questions get booked into a consult with our herbalist. You won't be thrown to the wolves. While you're learning, you can pass any hard call to our head herbalist, then listen to the recording afterward to hear how she handled it. We train this deeply because we want you here for years. What you'll do - Read and reply to customer service email s - Reply to customer text messages - Help customers place orders, track shipments, and resolve order issues - Set up appointments with our head herbalist for customers who want a deeper conversation about their dog - Study our knowledge base and keep learning. The more you know, the more you can help. - Answer phone calls when they come in. Some days are busier than others, but whenever the phone rings, that's your first priority. Who you are - Your English is clear with a neutral accent. Have past US customers ever been surprised to find out you weren't based in the US? If yes, please tell us about it in your application. Most of our customers are older American women (ages 40-65). They need to understand you the first time, every time. - Warm and patient on the phone. You sound like someone who could comfort a worried grandma. - A genuine dog lover. You'll be talking about dogs all day, every day: their names, their ages, their conditions, their quirks. - Hungry to learn. We'll hand you real training on herbal pet care, and we want someone who actually wants that knowledge and will use it to help people. - Kind during hard conversations. Sometimes a customer will tell you her dog was just diagnosed with something serious, or has just passed away. We don't expect you to have medical answers. We want you to be kind, slow down, listen, and let her know you understand. - Reliable. You show up on time, you follow up, you finish what you start, you don't drop the ball. - Comfortable with technology. You don't need to know our specific tools. We'll train you on those. If you already know any customer service, e-commerce, or admin tools, list them in your application. Requirements - Customer service experience helps but is optional. Clear, neutral English is required. - Reliable home internet with at least 25 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, and ping under 50ms, on a wired Ethernet connection (not WiFi alone). - A quiet home office. No background noise on calls: no roosters, no traffic, no kids, no neighbors. Backup power or a hotspot in case of outages is a strong plus. - Quality USB headset with a noise-cancelling microphone - Modern computer (Windows or Mac, less than 5 years old) - Available 9:00am to 5:00pm US Eastern Time, Monday to Friday. That's 9:00pm to 5:00am Philippines time. Please only apply if you can genuinely commit to that overnight schedule, long-term. - ID Proof verified on your OnlineJobs.ph profile. We only review applications from ID-verified accounts. Nice to have - You've worked for a small US-based e-commerce brand answering US customers, and those customers never realized you weren't based in the US. This is the experience we value most. - Familiarity with any customer service or e-commerce tools (Richpanel, helpdesks, e-comm platforms, email tools). List anything you've used. - Other work skills that could help a small company: bookkeeping, admin, writing, social media, scheduling, anything you do well. Schedule and pay - Full-time, 40 hours per week - Paid twice monthly - Long-term role. We're hiring carefully because we want to grow with the right person. How to apply (please read carefully, incomplete applications will not be reviewed) In your email , please include all 5 items below. We sort applications by who followed every instruction, not by who applied first. 1. At the very top of your email , write the word "Buddy" in bold. (This is so we know you read all the way to the end of this post.) 2. Record a 1 to 3 minute video covering the four prompts below, and get it to us any way you want: attach the file, paste a YouTube unlisted link, Google Drive, Dropbox, WeTransfer, anything that works. 3. Attach a screenshot of a current speedtest.net result showing your download speed, upload speed, and ping. In the email , also tell us what internet plan you have at home and whether you're on a wired Ethernet connection or WiFi. 4. List any customer service, e-commerce, admin, or office software you have used (for example: Richpanel, Gorgias, Zendesk, Help Scout, Shopify, WooCommerce, Klaviyo, QuickBooks, Google Workspace, anything you actually know). If you've never used any, write "none yet." That's an acceptable answer. 5. List one or more previous employers, teachers, clients, or anyone you've worked for who can speak to your work and character. Customer service references are best if you have them. One is fine if that's all you have. Video prompts (1 to 3 minutes total, single take, no editing) Cover all four, in any order. No script. Just talk to us like you'd talk to a customer. 1. Introduce yourself. Your first name, where you live in the Philippines, and one thing about you that's not on your resume. 2. Tell us about any experience helping people. Customer service if you have it, but teaching, retail, nursing, caring for family, anything where someone needed you and you showed up. If you can, tell us about one specific person you helped and what you did for them. 3. Tell us about a dog you've loved. Yours, a family dog, a neighbor's dog, any dog that mattered to you. What was their name, and what do you remember about them? 4. What else can you do? Customer service is the main job, but extra skills are gold to a small team like ours. Bookkeeping, admin, writing, social media, scheduling, anything you do well. If helping customers is your only area, just say so. That's a fine answer. Tips: - Record in a quiet room. Audio clarity matters more than video quality. - Use your phone or webcam. We want to hear the real you. - 1 minute minimum, 3 minutes maximum. Going under or over is a soft red flag. It tells us how you'd manage time on a real call. If your application is missing any of items 1 to 5, we will not review it. We're being strict because we're hiring carefully, and because the right person deserves a fair, fast review. After we watch your video and read your application, we'll reach out if we like you. At that point we'll ask you to obtain an NBI Clearance, and we'll reimburse the fee.

title: Product & Category Analyst / Market Research Specialist
job_title: Product & Category Analyst / Market Research Specialist
description: E-commerce on Bol · Remote · 3–4 days a week to start, growing as the role does We're a Dutch e-commerce business selling on the Bol marketplace, and we're growing fast. A big part of that growth comes down to one hard question, asked over and over: what should we launch next, and what should we leave alone? Most people get this wrong. They chase trends, ignore the margin, and miss the products that quietly print money. We're looking for the person who gets it right more often than not. This isn't a research-assistant job. You won't be filling in sheets someone else acts on. You'll be the one finding the opportunities, weighing them honestly, and putting your name to a recommendation. You'd work directly with me, the founder, alongside our data analyst and purchasing team. You bring the thinking, we d ---------- together, and you watch your calls play out in the business. What you'd be doing There are three sides to this role. Finding new products to launch. This is the heart of the job. We aim to launch around five new product keywords a month (each one usually having 2-3 SKUs). You'd hunt for those opportunities, run them through clear criteria, and bring me a short, well-argued case for each one worth pursuing. You'd also check the sourcing data our purchasing team gathers, so we're confident the numbers behind a launch actually hold up. Growing what we already sell. Looking at our existing products and finding ways to do better, a smart addition to a product family, a sharper price, better quality, a stronger look. You'd spot where we can extend or improve an offer and make the case for it. Trends and seasonality. Keeping an eye on where the market's heading, and working closely with our data analyst to flag seasonal swings before they hit, Q4 build-ups, summer or winter spikes on certain SKUs, and which categories are growing or shrinking year on year. Your job is to make sure we're never caught off guard on timing. How we think about a good product We have criteria, and part of your job is to apply them sharply: enough demand to be worth it, competition we can realistically beat, and margin that still works after all marketplace costs and sourcing. Those are the filters. The judgment, which of the products that clear those filters is actually worth launching, is the part we're hiring you for. We can teach you our thresholds. We can't teach instinct, so that's what we'll be looking for, and we'll know quickly whether you have it. Who we're hoping to find Real e-commerce and marketplace research experience. (at least 3 years / preferably 5+) You've done product research for an online business before, ideally on a marketplace like Bol, Amazon, or similar marketplaces. You understand how demand, competition, reviews, pricing, and fulfilment costs come together to make a product win or lose. Judgment that's been proven, not just claimed. Anyone can pull numbers and call something "trending." We need someone who looks at a category and knows which gap is a real opportunity and which is a trap that'll cost us money. If you've actually launched or recommended products that worked, that's what we want to hear about. Comfortable with the tools. Bol's own data, marketplace research tools (Helium 10, Keepa, or similar specific for Bol like Marktmentor), and AI tools for speeding up research and analysis. If you already lean on AI to work faster and sharper, you'll fit right in. A close collaborator. You'll work hand in hand with our data analyst and purchasing team, so you need to communicate clearly and share what you find in a way others can act on. Fully fluent English, happy working remotely with a few hours of daily overlap with European time. What you get out of it -Real ownership. You're not a research assistant filling sheets, you own product discovery and shape what we launch. Your work is visible in the business fast. -A direct line to the founder. You bring the opportunities, we d ---------- together, and you see your calls play out. -Room to grow. This starts at 3–4 days a week and can grow with the company as our launch pace picks up. -A company that invests in you. We're built on quality, in our products, our service, and the life of our team. We back that with a monthly health bonus you can put toward whatever keeps you well, gym, better sleep, whatever works for you. -Remote, wherever you are, with just a few hours of daily overlap with European time. -USD $15 an hour to start, with real room to move up as you prove yourself. How to apply Skip the long CV for now. Instead, I'd like to see how you actually work. Pick any product category you like and find me three products you'd consider worth launching on a marketplace. For each one, tell me briefly why, what makes you think there's a real opportunity, and what would make you nervous about it. I'm not expecting it to match our business perfectly, I want to see how you spot and weigh an opportunity. Then tell me a little about your background in e-commerce research, and what made you want this role specifically. One last thing. We're after real A-players, and A-players like to work with other A-players. So if you've read this and thought "yes, this is me", apply. I'm looking forward to seeing what you find.

title: Freelance Inventory Planner — Ecommerce
description: Hi! We are a fast-growing Dutch premium ecommerce brand selling scented products online. We are scaling quickly and need someone who can help us stay on top of our inventory, so we never run out of stock. What this job is: - We are looking for a freelance inventory planner who can build a forecasting system and give us weekly advice on our stock levels. - This is not a supply chain management role. You will not contact suppliers. You will not place orders. We handle all of that ourselves. Your job is simple: - Receive data from us (Shopify exports, current stock levels, lead time updates) - Build a model that calculates when we need to reorder each product - Tell us what to order, how much, and when, before we run out Phase 1 — Build the system (first 2–4 weeks, approximately 8–10 hours per week) - Aalyse our currect system - Map all our products and current stock levels - Analyze sales velocity per SKU - Build a reorder model in Excel or Google Sheets (or something like that) that calculates reorder points, safety stock, and projected stock-out dates - Account for variable supplier lead times, we will always tell you when lead times change - Deliver a clean, easy-to-read dashboard that shows us what action to take each week - Document everything so we always understand the model Phase 2 — Ongoing management (after setup, approximately 2–4 hours per week)** - Update the forecast 1–2 times per week based on our latest sales data - Send us a short weekly update: what needs to be ordered, what is at risk, what is fine - Adjust forecasts when we inform you about upcoming sales, promotions, or lead time changes - Keep the model accurate and up to date Important: We always inform you about any changes that affect inventory: new sales campaigns, changed lead times, new products. You take that input and update the forecast accordingly. What we are looking for - Experience in inventory planning or demand forecasting for an ecommerce or product-based business - Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills — you must be comfortable building formulas, reorder models, and dashboards - Experience working with Shopify data (sales reports, inventory exports) - Clear and structured communicator — your weekly update must be simple and direct, not a complex report - Reliable and proactive — you flag risks before they become problems AI and automation bonus We actively reward smart use of AI tools. If you can automate parts of the forecasting process — for example using AI to process Shopify exports, generate forecast updates, or flag reorder ---------- nts automatically — you will be compensated better for it. Tell us in your application what you have automated before and how. Tools we currently use - Excel with manual Shopify exports - You may propose a better system if you have experience with tools like Inventory Planner, Stocky, or similar, but Excel or Google Sheets is fine Practical details - Freelance, part-time, fully remote - Phase 1: approximately 8–10 hours per week for 2–4 weeks - Phase 2: approximately 2–4 hours per week, ongoing - Pay: will be discussed based of the workload - Pay is bi-weekly or monthly --- How to apply — read this carefully To submit a valid application, your message must include all four of the following: 1. Start your message with the word: REORDER,  applications that do not start with this word will not be reviewed 2. Describe one specific inventory or forecasting system you have built before — what was the business, what did you build, and what tool did you use 3. Tell us which tools you currently work with most (Excel, Google Sheets, Inventory Planner, or other) 4. Tell us in 1–2 sentences: what is the biggest risk when a fast-growing ecommerce brand does not have a proper reorder system? 4. Tell us how you would use AI o build the system or automate certain processes? Applications that do not follow these instructions will be skipped automatically.

title: Business / Finance Controller (Remote)
description: WDM | E-commerce on Bol | Remote | 3–4 days per week (path to full-time as we grow) We're a Dutch e-commerce business selling on the Bol marketplace. We're small, we move fast, and we've automated a lot of the heavy lifting, including our P&L and cashflow, which now run on AI-driven models. So we're not looking for someone to put reports together. We already have the numbers. What we don't have yet is the person who looks at those numbers and d ---------- what we should actually do about them. That's the role. You'd work directly with me, the founder. When margin slips, you're the one who figures out why and what to change. When we're sitting on overstock, you're the one who d ---------- what to clear, at what price, and when, and backs it with the maths. When our models spit out a suggestion, you're the one who checks whether it's actually right before we act on it. What you'd own -Margin. Track it across products and channels, work out what's driving it up or down, and drive the changes that protect it. -Commercial decisions. Turn the data and the model output into real calls on pricing, promotions, assortment, and inventory. -Overstock. Treat it as a financial decision, not a guess. Put a number on it and d ---------- how and when to clear it. -A check on the models. Pressure-test what our AI finance tools produce before we trust it. The model proposes, you validate, I d ---------- . -SKU profitability. Find the winners and the quiet money-losers, and turn that into pricing and assortment decisions. The formal finance side. VAT, year-end, the accountant, compliance, and being in the room for any banking or financing conversations. -Cashflow. Keep an eye on the position, flag risks early, and understand how purchasing and stock decisions hit working capital. What it isn't A heads-up so we don't waste each other's time. This isn't a bookkeeping or monthly-reporting job, our systems already handle that. You also won't be building or fixing the data pipelines; we have a data analyst who owns data accuracy, and you'd work alongside them as an equal. Note: it might be that you spot these and work allong side the data analist to tackle bugs. Nobody's going to hand you a task list. You're the one making the calls. Who we're hoping to find The thing that's rare, and the thing we really want, is someone who has the Skills to equally handle P&L/Cashflow, can make SKU-level margin breakdowns, and can make decision messy stock data. Most finance people are only comfortable with the first; most data people only the last. We need someone who bridges all three. Example of decision comming from this -Pay of loans x amount of weeks -Push these products to gain turnover or lower overstock -Invest in these categories or when we are ready to invest in growth -Prep for Q4 financially and on SKU level. -Tips on lowering Opperational expenditure (where is the biggest cash leak and a step by step on how to fix it) Marketplace experience matters to us more than a long corporate finance CV. If you understand how fulfilment costs, returns, ad spend, and tied-up inventory eat into margin, you'll be of great impact from week one. We care more about how you think than how many years you've done it. A sharp person with three to five years and real commercial instinct beats someone with a longer history who's only ever produced reports. What we're really after is someone who's owned decisions, not just numbers, and who's comfortable telling me I'm wrong when the data says so. You'll need to be fluent in English, happy working remotely with a few hours of daily overlap with European time, and comfortable working with AI-driven finance tools and a modern e-commerce stack. What you get out of it -Real ownership from day one. You're not slotting into a process, you're shaping how we make decisions. -The finance and data side of the business is yours to lead. -A direct line to the founder. No layers, no politics. You bring the thinking, we d ---------- together, and you see your calls play out in the business fast. -Room to grow. This starts at 3–4 days a week and grows into a full-time leadership seat as we scale. Get this right and the role grows with the company. -A company that invests in you. We're built on quality, not just in our products and service, but in the life of our team. We back that up with a monthly health bonus you can put toward whatever keeps you well, gym, better sleep, whatever works for you. If we expect quality from you, we owe you the conditions to deliver it. -Remote, wherever you are, with just a few hours of daily overlap with European time. -USD $15–$20 an hour to start, with real room to move up as you prove yourself. How to apply Skip the long CV for now. Instead, I'd like a few things in your own words. First, tell me how you'd think about this: say we've got a chunk of capital tied up in overstock. How would you d ---------- what to clear, at what price, and when? I'm not after a perfect answer, you don't know our data yet, I just want to see how your mind works on it. Then share a quick story about a time you pushed back on a number, a model, or a boss, and how it played out. And tell me a little about what you've done before, and what made you want this role specifically. One last thing. We're after real A-players, and A-players like to work with other A-players. So if you've read this and thought yes, this is me, apply. I'm looking forward to reading it.

title: Account & Driver Partnership Specialist
description: Hiring Filipino and Philippine-based professionals only! Wingz, is a leading US rideshare company focused on Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT). Visit our website: ---------- Position: Account & Driver Partnership Specialist Work Schedule: US Hours (EST) Employment Set-up: Remote (Independent Contractor) Employment Type: Full-Time / Long Term Salary Range: USD 1,200 - 1,800 / Month Benefit: PTO and HMO after the 120-day probationary period Pay-out Frequency: Semi-monthly Equipment: Self-Provide Performance Bonus: Starts at approximately USD 300–700 per month on average, with potential for higher earnings based on performance. You'll start by learning that market inside and out, its clients, its drivers, its trip patterns, and from there, you'll wear two hats every day. Both are essential to how Wingz works. On the client side, you'll act as the dedicated account manager for our partnered NEMT brokers, the organizations that send trip requests for their members. You'll handle daily B2B communication, trip coordination, escalation management, and performance reporting. Your job is to build a strong partnership with each broker and earn their trust until Wingz is their most reliable carrier in the market. That trust matters — it's what causes brokers to route more trips to us. And once they do, you'll own the commitment to make sure every assigned trip gets completed safely and on time. On the driver side, you'll own the full driver lifecycle in your market, recruitment, onboarding, activation, engagement, and retention. That means walking new drivers through every requirement, procedure, and process so they can confidently join the NEMT industry with Wingz. It means proactively reaching out to inactive drivers and reactivating them. It means being the human point of contact that keeps drivers engaged, earning, and partnered with us long-term — because retention isn't built on incentives, it's built on relationships. This is a foundational individual-contributor role, by design. You'll start at the rank-and-file level because the path forward at Wingz is clear: Specialist ? Senior Specialist ? Market Lead. We're not hiring for a job; we're hiring for a career, and the people who learn the Wingz foundation now are the leaders we promote into the next phase of growth. Key Responsibilities: • Learn your market first. Get to know the clients, the drivers, the trip patterns, and the relationships that make your assigned market work; your fluency here is the foundation for everything else. • Build strong partnerships with our NEMT broker clients. Show up consistently, communicate clearly, and follow through every time. Your goal is to make Wingz the trusted, reliable carrier in your market, so brokers route more trips to us. • Commit to trip completion. Once a trip is assigned to Wingz, you own it. Coordinate with drivers, monitor trips in progress, and resolve issues quickly so every member gets to their appointment safely and on time. • Onboard new drivers into the Wingz partnership. Walk them through every requirement, procedure, and process, documentation, background checks, vehicle readiness, so they can confidently join the NEMT industry as a Wingz partner driver. • Activate inactive drivers. Make the calls, understand what's holding them back, and get them back on the road. • Drive partner-driver success. Be the human point of contact our drivers can count on. Build loyalty, prevent churn, and grow retention in your market, because every retained driver is one we don't have to replace. • Help drivers grow their daily earnings. Where needed, coordinate trip assignments and dispatch so your drivers see consistent, meaningful daily income. Strong earnings are what keep drivers partnered with Wingz long-term. • Step into adjacent responsibilities as the team scales, operations support, dispatch backup, training new hires, and wherever the business needs you most. • Bring market-level insights back to the wider Wingz team to inform how we improve. Qualifications: • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience. title: Shopify Website Administrator
description: About us We are a US-based e-commerce company in the tabletop roleplaying games (TTRPG) accessory space. We design and sell our products direct to consumers and through retail partners worldwide. The role We need a detail-oriented Shopify administrator for roughly one day of work per week. You will post new products, audit the site for problems, and build static informational pages. The schedule is flexible, we care that the work gets done well each week, not which day you do it. For the right person with broader Shopify skills, this role can grow. What you will do •       Post new products to our Shopify store: photos, descriptions, variants, pricing, and collections. •       Review the website weekly for errors: missing product photos, broken links, formatting problems, and out-of-date content. •       Monthly review of out-of-stock products with summary sent to leadership. •       Apply SEO best practices to product pages: titles, meta descriptions, alt text, and keywords. •       Build and maintain static informational pages (FAQ, events, policies, product guides). Must-haves •       Hands-on Shopify experience: posting products, editing pages, and managing collections. •       Strong attention to detail - you catch the missing photo, typo or small details that nobody else notices. •       Working knowledge of on-page SEO best practices. •       Reliable and consistent: this is a small weekly commitment, and we need it done every week without reminders. •       Strong communication skills: being able to clearly summarize your accomplished tasks and progress is required, and engage in productive discussions to fully understand tasks and projects •       Strong organizational skills: all tasks must be clearly organized with progress tracked, using our project management software (Click Up) and additional tools such as google sheets where needed •       Understand the vision, not just the steps: you should clearly understand the goals of your projects in order to suggest best practices, process, or detail changes, in order to achieve the best results Nice-to-haves (not required) •       Shopify programming experience (Liquid, theme customization). •       Shopify Flow experience and a general knack for automating repetitive tasks. Tools you will use Shopify, ClickUp, Google Workspace. How we work •       All work is managed in ClickUp. Every task has a clear deliverable and due date, you will always know exactly what is expected and when. In return we expect you to use this tool to properly communicate your work, needs and questions. We measure output, not hours of activity. Finished quality deliverables are what count. •       Communication is in writing first (ClickUp comments and email ), with a weekly tea ---------- eting video call. •       We expect a few hours of overlap with US business hours for communication; the rest of your schedule is flexible. How to apply Start your application with the word WRENCH so we know you read this posting. Then include: •       Links to 2–3 Shopify stores you have worked on and what you did on each. •       A video or written explanation of your experience for this position and why you would be good for this role. •       Your expected hourly rate. Applications that do not follow these instructions will not be considered.

title: Marketing Director
description: BUILT. — Marketing Coordinator Full-Time Remote | Philippines-Based | $1,200–$2,000/month What BUILT. is BUILT. is a six-week live referral implementation program for real estate agents and mortgage loan officers. Participants arrive with a database. They leave with a referral system running across email , text, and ringless voi cemail — built, loaded, and active before the program ends. The program is a joint venture between Shon Kokoszka (ICON Coaching) and Dan Stewart (Happy Grasshopper). We are in active growth: first cohort live, enterprise partnerships in motion, and a coach certification program in development. What this role is This is not a social media job. It is not a graphic design job. It is a coordination role for someone who can hold multiple complex workstreams together simultaneously, enforce brand and copy standards without being asked twice, and keep assets, vendors, and deadlines moving without constant direction from the founders. You will work directly with Shon. You will coordinate with a small group of key people: a dashboard developer, a web integrations specialist, an enterprise business development lead, and the Happy Grasshopper platform team. What you will own Project coordination across all active BUILT. build workstreams — sessions, workbooks, legal documents, enterprise materials, coach program infrastructure, and digital assets. You track what exists, what is in progress, and what is missing, and you keep it moving. Email marketing and platform tools — you will work inside Happy Grasshopper and ActiveCampaign, coordinating sequence builds, participant communications, and enrollment follow-up. You do not need to be a developer, but you need to be comfortable in platforms and learn new ones quickly. Copy and brand standards enforcement — every piece of BUILT. material that goes out passes through you. You know the rules: no em dashes, the period in BUILT. is always present, no coaching clichés, no negative headlines, Brass is the only accent color. You catch violations before they ship. Digital asset management — you will handle HTML files, Canva assets, StackWrap dashboard tiles, workbook PDFs, pull-up banners, and social cards. You organize them, version them, and make sure the right files get to the right people. What this role is not This is not a role where you wait for instructions. If something is blocking a deliverable, you surface it and propose a solution. If a file is missing, you track it down. If a deadline is at risk, you flag it before it slips, not after. What you need 4+ years of experience in a marketing, operations, or executive support role — ideally supporting founders or small teams with multiple simultaneous projects. Demonstrated experience with email marketing platforms (Happy Grasshopper, ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, or equivalent). Strong written English — C1 or C2 level. You will be reviewing copy for correctness and brand voice, not just formatting. Comfort with digital files in multiple formats: HTML, PDF, Canva, Google Sheets, and basic CRM tools. High attention to detail. You will be tested on this. The brand has hard rules and they exist for a reason. What will make you stand out Experience supporting a coaching, training, or real estate company. Familiarity with Canva and light graphic production. Experience with Zapier or similar workflow automation tools. How to apply Send your application to ---------- with the subject line: BUILT. Coordinator — [Your Name]. In your message, answer these three questions in plain prose (no bullet points): Describe a situation where you were coordinating multiple workstreams for a founder or executive and something fell through the cracks. What happened and what did you change? What email marketing platform are you most experienced with, and what specifically have you built or managed inside it? The BUILT. brand has a hard rule: no em dashes, ever. Rewrite this sentence without using one: "The system runs whether you feel like it or not — that's the point." Applications that do not answer all three questions will not be reviewed.

job_title: HR Director — Home Health Agency (Talent, Compliance & Caregiver Retention)
description: ABOUT THE ROLE We're a growing home health agency in Ohio looking for an exceptional HR Director to own our people function end-to-end — recruiting, onboarding, compliance, retention, employee relations, and the systems that hold it all together. Caregiver turnover is the single biggest challenge in our industry. If you've moved that number at a previous home health, home care, hospice, or skilled nursing employer, you're who we want to talk to. This is a remote, full-time, senior seat. You'll be the most senior HR voice in the company, working directly with the CEO and operations leadership. The work is high-trust, high-judgment, and high-impact. We're hiring one person — we want it to be the right person. WHAT YOU'LL OWN: - Full-cycle recruiting for clinical (RN, LPN, PT/OT/ST, HHA, caregiver) and administrative roles — including agency partnerships, job board strategy, and proactive sourcing - Onboarding and credentialing — license verification, OIG/SAM exclusion checks, background and drug screens, I-9, BLS, TB, and home-health-specific training records - Multi-state HR compliance — federal DOL (FLSA, FMLA, ADA, companionship exemption rules), state nursing board and home health regulations, EEO/OFCCP, workers' comp, OSHA, and applicable state-level paid sick / paid family leave laws - HIPAA training program ownership — annual training, attestation tracking, sanction policy, audit-ready documentation - Policy and employee handbook authorship — readable, defensible, and updated when the law moves - HRIS, ATS, and payroll system administration (Paychex, ADP, Paylocity, BambooHR, Workable, Greenhouse, or comparable) - Employee relations and investigations — handled with discretion, documentation, and clean judgment - Performance management framework — coaching managers, running review cycles, structuring PIPs that hold up - Benefits administration — open enrollment, broker management, COBRA, retirement plan coordination - Workers' comp claim management — return-to-work coordination, OSHA 300 logs, i ---------- root-cause work - Turnover analytics — own the dashboard, present root causes monthly, drive the retention strategy - Stay-interview and exit-interview programs that produce real insight, not paperwork WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR: - Minimum 5 years of progressive HR experience, including at least 2 years in a senior or director-level seat - Direct home health, home care, hospice, post-acute, or skilled nursing HR experience is REQUIRED — not a "plus." This industry has rules that take years to learn. - SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR certification (or active, documented progress toward one) - Demonstrated track record of reducing caregiver or clinical-staff turnover at a previous employer — be ready to talk specific numbers - Working knowledge of CMS Conditions of Participation for home health, OASIS workflows, and Medicare/Medicaid compliance touchpoints that intersect with HR - Hands-on experience with HRIS / ATS / payroll platforms (Paychex, ADP, Paylocity, BambooHR, Workable, Greenhouse, or similar) - Bulletproof written English — you'll author policies, handbooks, investigation memos, and disciplinary documentation that have to stand up to legal scrutiny - Calm, confidential, and decisive in employee relations situations - Comfortable being the senior HR voice in the company and pushing back on the CEO when the law or the policy requires it - Comfortable signing an NDA and completing HIPAA training before day one WORK ENVIRONMENT (NON-NEGOTIABLE): - Reliable high-speed internet (minimum 25 Mbps down / 10 Mbps up) - Quiet, professional workspace - USB headset and a working webcam - A primary device on supported OS (Windows 11 or macOS) SCHEDULE AND COMPENSATION: - Full-time, 40 hours/week - Eastern Time business hours, primary overlap 9 AM – 5 PM ET - $8–10 USD/hour, depending on experience and certifications - 10 paid days off per year - Annual performance review with a defined raise framework DO NOT APPLY IF: - You don't have direct home health, home care, hospice, post-acute, or skilled nursing HR experience - You're currently juggling another full-time role - You're more comfortable executing tactics than owning strategy — this is a director seat, not a coordinator role - You're not comfortable with confidential information, NDAs, or HIPAA-style training HOW TO APPLY: Send the following: 1. Your résumé. 2. A brief written description (3–6 sentences) telling us why you'd be a great fit for this specific role. 3. A short video (1–2 minutes) telling us why you're the best person for this and what sets you apart from the others. 4. A short story (5–8 sentences) about a specific turnover or retention problem you solved at a previous employer — what the metric was before, what you changed, what the metric was after, and how long it took. This is the instinct we're hiring for. You MUST submit a video. Your application subject line MUST include the exact phrase: "Your problems are over". We use a paid trial. Top applicants will be invited to a paid trial task (10–15 hours, compensated) that mirrors the real work — a sample handbook policy authorship exercise and a turnover-analytics dashboard build using anonymized data we provide. We make hires only after the trial.
